2326985.title: English rendering of PM's address in NDTV World Summit
2326985.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM's address in NDTV World Summit
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 9:32PM by PIB Delhi

Greetings to all of you! This is the festive season; the nation is filled with celebration, enthusiasm, and energy. In this atmosphere of joy and celebration, I welcome and greet all of you friends who have come here from all over the world.

Friends,

This NDTV summit is dedicated to deliberating on serious matters. Nowadays, everyone is talking about a new world order. Because this affects ordinary life, the importance of such world summits increases even more.

Friends

When talking about 'The World Between Orders', we need to understand two things. First, why is the world order changing? Why is the old global order unable to provide solutions to today's challenges? And second, what is India's role in this changing world?

Friends,

If I elaborate on the first point, this change is natural and spontaneous. The Second World War taught the world a major lesson. The world realized that a global order cannot function merely on the basis of power and self-interest. Dialogue is essential, cooperation is necessary, and resolving disputes is equally vital. It was this sentiment that laid the foundation of the United Nations, or the UN. For decades, the UN played a significant role in promoting global cooperation and peace. But with time, the world kept changing. New aspirations emerged. New economies and new powers arose. The challenges confronting the world also became far more complex than ever before. Technology transformed society, the economy, and the very nature of power. And countries that were not at the table when the global order was initially established came forward with their own prominent roles. The question then arises: did the global order change at the same pace? The answer is no. Neither did the world order change, nor could global institutions adapt themselves with equivalent speed. The United Nations and other global institutions have had their historic role. Yet in the face of today’s challenges, their limitations are clearly visible. Now, emerging powers are rising. New voices are demanding their rightful place. New challenges demand new solutions. When the reality of the world shifts, but decision-making methods remain unchanged, a gap begins to widen between the system and reality. That is precisely what we are witnessing today. For decades, trade connected nations, technology closed distances, maritime routes linked economies, and culture and mobility brought diverse societies closer together; but today, these very links face fresh strains. Trade is being weaponized. Technology is turning into a new arena of competition and conflict. Sea routes are emerging as epicenters of geopolitical tension. Therefore, the challenge today is not merely about the emergence of a new global order. The real challenge is: in a changing world, how do we build an order where new realities find their place, global institutions become more effective, and the spirit of cooperation among nations is reinforced? And this is where the question of India's role comes to the fore.

Friends,

Before elaborating on India's role, I will take you back by 7 to 8 years. What transpired during the COVID pandemic is something we all witnessed. When the world needed cooperation the most, it appeared completely divided. Those who made grand proclamations about globalization prioritized their own self-interests in a time of crisis. In that era of fragmentation, everyone viewed each other with suspicion, and global trust had hit rock bottom; it was then, in 2020, from the G20 platform, that I placed an idea before the world, calling for "a new world order for the collective well-being of humankind" - an order with humanity at its very core. That same year, from the UNGA platform, I said, "If the century changes and we do not, our ability to bring about change also weakens."

Friends,

Today, while it is true that the world order is changing, the real question is: as the old global order shifts, what kind of new world order do we want to build together? Reforms in multilateral institutions are essential. It is vital to grant the Global South its rightful place and voice. International cooperation must not be reserved only for good times; it must remain effective during crises, and for this, meaningful consensus among all stakeholders is imperative.

Friends,

In our heritage, Chanakya stated in the Arthashastra: ‘Apranitah tu matsya-nyayam ud-bhavayati’ - meaning, when governance weakens, the "law of the fish" (matsya nyaya) takes over. Under matsya nyaya, the big fish swallows the smaller fish. The world needs a system that prevents such a situation from arising. That is India's vision, and that is precisely what India is doing. The world experienced this role of India during the severe crisis of the pandemic. When capable nations were thinking solely of themselves, India stepped forward, delivered vaccines to every needy nation, and dispatched medicines to over 100 countries.

Friends,

Guided by the principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’, India is performing its duty as a Vishwa-Bandhu (universal friend). You have witnessed this firsthand: the G20 Summit was held under India’s presidency, and the BRICS Summit was held under India’s leadership. How many doubts were voiced regarding both summits? It was said that building consensus on joint declarations would be impossible. But India built bridges, emphasized dialogue, and on both occasions, the Delhi Declaration was adopted through unanimous consensus. Nations considered bitter rivals came together on India’s platform. This is not mere coincidence. This is the trust placed in India’s role as a Vishwa-Bandhu.

Friends,

The stronger and more empowered India becomes, the greater the benefit to humanity. This is because India's policies and decisions are inspired by timeless experience and civilizational values. India does not make decisions driven by fleeting moments. Hence, India is a guarantee of stability and an assurance of continuity. Our resolve for a Viksit Bharat (Developed India) also fosters this very spirit. Just a few days ago at a summit, I presented the vision of "Power to Empower." A developed India is not just for ourselves; it is a guarantee for a better world. When India advances toward self-reliance, it strengthens global supply chains. When India's economy grows stronger, it provides hope of prosperity to the world. When India’s youth become capable and skilled, it inspires global confidence in innovation and productivity. In other words, India is enhancing its own capabilities today so that the world’s capacity can also increase.

Friends,

India is working with all its might to become a top-3 economy. Our confidence grows even further when we look at the present difficult global circumstances, in the midst of which India continues to emerge as the fastest-growing major economy. Today, India is among the top economies in green energy. India ranks among the top three AI ecosystems. India is among the top three startup ecosystems. India is one of the largest digital economies. India stands number one in real-time digital payments.

Friends,

Today's India is expanding its capabilities across various sectors, and there are numerous milestones achieved for the first time in the country. India's Fast Breeder Reactor achieved criticality for the first time. India linked the Census with digital technology for the first time. During this period, India’s first hydrogen train began operations, and India crossed the 300-gigawatt mark in non-fossil electricity capacity for the first time.

Friends,

I will give you another example. A few days ago, I had the opportunity to meet young athletes returning from the Asian Games. India won 85 medals this time, achieving many milestones for the first time. The women’s recurve archery team won team and individual gold medals for the first time. In boxing, India won three gold medals in a single Asian Games, which is also a first.

Friends,

Now I will mention a term, and I hope many people in the hall have heard it. The word is - Sepak Takraw. Sepak Takraw, have you heard this word? For those who do not know, let me tell you that it is the name of a sport. The world plays it and has been winning medals in it. It is essentially a hybrid combination of football and volleyball. It is played with the feet, but the action takes place across a net. India won a medal for the first time in recent Asian Games in an event of this sport - the Men’s Quadrant.

Friends,

This is the hallmark of a changing India. In every sector, something new and unprecedented is taking place. That means India's conventional strengths are being reinforced, and where we were once not as strong, we are emerging as a new force. None of this is happening in isolation; it is the direct outcome of the policy of 'Reform, Perform, Transform'.

Friends,

The country has seen days when the entire power grid would collapse under rising electricity demand. But when a nation rises with sheer willpower and sets forth, the power grid does not collapse; instead, that very grid fuels the nation's progress and soaring confidence.

Friends,

Today, our youth power, women power, our farmers, fishermen, the poor, and the middle class are engaged with high spirits in the building of a Viksit Bharat. Look around today: India's exports are setting new records. Speaking of September alone, exports of goods and products increased by nearly 25 percent compared to last year. Seafood exports have more than doubled in the last 12 years. In our villages, more than 3.5 crore women have become Lakhpati Didis, and we are working toward the goal of creating 6 crore Lakhpati Didis. Under the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana, around 70 lakh new jobs have been created in a very short span of time. For the middle class, income tax has been made zero up to 12 lakh rupees - this needs to be reminded to you again and again; it cannot be that you simply take what you get and forget it. Ease of Living is improving across the country, and new employment opportunities are being generated.

Friends,

There was a time when the world referred to India as the 'World’s Back Office', but today's India is not merely a service provider; we are innovating, designing, and creating new solutions and technologies for the world. Look at the field of research alone: today we rank third in research publications. In the year 2025, nearly 1.5 lakh patents were filed - 1.5 lakh patents in a single year. This offers a glimpse into the immense potential for research and innovation in India.

Friends,

Consider the semiconductor sector as well: nearly 20 percent of the world’s chip-design workforce is in India. Indian engineers within the country are working on advanced 2 to 3-nanometer chip designs. To expand this talent pool further, every necessary facility is being provided in the country today. In Indian academic institutions, our students have designed more than 325 chips so far.

Friends,

Another example is Global Capability Centres. More than half of the world’s capability centres are located in India. It is not just about the numbers; the nature of their work is changing. Previously, many centres focused solely on support services. Today, they operate across fields like AI, Cloud, Engineering, Analytics, and Product Development. In other words, India’s role is shifting, and India’s identity is evolving. We have moved from 'Talent at Scale' to 'Thinking at Scale'. The world that once trusted India’s manpower now places equal trust in India’s mind-power. As a result, we are working alongside the world not merely as a Back Office, but as a Brain Office.

Friends,

Whenever the government frames a policy or takes an investment decision in any sector, there is clear thinking behind it: what capacities India needs to develop, in which domains we must reduce dependence on other nations, and which impending crises we must prepare for today. We keep these factors in mind with every decision. There are many investments whose benefits take years to become visible, but they hold immense significance for the nation's future. Let me share an interesting example. All of you are familiar with India's pharmaceutical capabilities, but until a few years ago, India relied heavily on imports for raw materials and medicines. Now the country is changing this situation. You must have heard of Penicillin G, which is essential for antibiotics. Over the last two to three decades, its domestic production in India had practically ceased. We brought it under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme. Today, after many years, domestic production of Penicillin G has resumed in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh.

Friends,

Penicillin G is just one example. In India, we are building an entire domestic supply chain for APIs (Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients) - the fundamental raw materials for medicine manufacturing. That is why this sector was brought under the PLI scheme, attracting over 5,000 crore rupees in investment so far, with around 40 projects already underway. Such policies and decisions are steering India toward self-reliance.

Friends,

Amidst discussions of so many national achievements, our media friends might complain that while much was said, nothing was spoken about their work. NDTV is hosting such a magnificent event, and our motto is ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ - which includes the development of the media - so perhaps you would appreciate a few candid and sweet-and-sour remarks as well?

Friends,

While the world is searching for a new order, some people are dreaming of disorder in India. Today, when there is so much disarray in the world, the image of a strong India should be conveyed globally. Yet these individuals are bent on tarnishing India's reputation. They travel abroad to defame India and plead for foreign intervention. One wonders how long Congress will continue to wager the nation's interests just to launch its failed product. In an entire year, Sriharikota does not attempt as many launches as Congress makes failed attempts to launch its leader.

Friends,

Whatever decline Congress chooses to bring upon itself is entirely its own concern, and we have no problem with that. But to protect one family from the repeated stain of failure, Congress is putting India's achievements, strengths, and progress on trial. The grapes are so sour that Congress has set about cutting down the grapevine itself. In reality, this family has become a burden on their party; senior elders of the party understand this and even share it with us in private, yet they swallow their humiliation and remain silent.

Friends,

This conduct of Congress harms honest critics of the government as well, and this imposes a huge cost in a democracy. Honest critics suffer immensely because of this. Those who wish to present their critique against the government in a democratic manner find their voices drowned out by Congress's clamour; the voices of genuine critics are suppressed. Those who genuinely care for democracy and the national interest—even if they are staunch opponents of the government—find no opportunity to speak amidst the shouting and screeching of Congress. We have seen in Parliament: there are so many talented young Members of Parliament from opposition parties who wish to put forward their views and critique the government, but Congress disrupts Parliament so that others do not get an opportunity, simply because Congress wants to keep only one person in the limelight. By doing so, Congress does a grave injustice to the young MPs of the opposition.

And friends,

Movements that organically aim to highlight the government’s shortcomings and genuinely seek systemic reform—which is indeed necessary in a democracy—are also ruined by Congress. Congress has become a parasite that does not want anyone else to progress. Intellectual Naxals have captured Congress's mind to such an extent that Congress has lost its own capacity to think. Those who once wrought destruction in forests have infiltrated Congress and are now bent on wreaking havoc on the country.

Friends,

Amidst all these challenges, the grand goal of a Viksit Bharat stands before us. The nation's aspirations are boundless. Therefore, a single spirit resonates across India today, and that spirit is: 'We Will Do It, We Will Do It.' We will dream big, turn every challenge into an opportunity, and translate every resolution into reality. Our strength is our self-confidence; our inspiration lies in the dreams of 140 crore fellow citizens. We will innovate, forge new paths, reach new heights, and link India's success with the world's success. I am confident that the nectar emerging from this summit will empower this very spirit, infuse our resolutions with new energy, and play a vital role in realizing India's grand aspirations. Once again, my warmest wishes to all of you.

Thank you very much.

DISCLAIMER: This is the approximate translation of Prime Minister’s address. Original address was delivered in Hindi.

2326933.title: “Save both people and fields”: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan launches nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from Taraori in Karnal
2326933.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
“Save both people and fields”: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan launches nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from Taraori in Karnal
“Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi feels deeply concerned about why our land and fields cannot remain healthy; protecting soil from becoming barren is our national duty”: Shri Shivraj Singh
Major rural development gift for Haryana: Permanent houses worth ₹1,343 crore approved for 28,422 poor families; Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh hands over the approval letter
“Nationwide campaign to run from 22 October to 30 November: Scientists will visit villages across the country to raise public awareness,” says Shri Shivraj Singh
“Affordable fertilisers do not mean indiscriminate use: Government provides relief to farmers through subsidies exceeding ₹1.5 lakh crore, but urea and DAP must be applied according to need,” says Shri Shivraj Singh
“Chemical fertilisers and pesticides are turning the human body into a breeding ground for diseases: Farmers should check Soil Health Cards before applying fertilisers and adopt balanced nutrient management,” says Shri Shivraj Singh
“Hardworking farmers of Haryana have shown a new path to the entire country: They are also transforming agriculture in Madhya Pradesh,” says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
“Green ammonia will make India self-reliant in fertiliser production: Adopt crop rotation and do not kill beneficial insects and earthworms by burning crop residue,” says Shri Shivraj Singh
“Start with at least half an acre: Adopt natural farming using Beejamrit and Ghanjeevamrit to reduce costs and increase yields,” says Shri Shivraj Singh
Farmers take a solemn collective pledge to use fertilisers in a balanced manner and protect their fields, raising slogans of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai” alongside Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh on the sacred land of Taraori
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today formally launched the nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from the historic town of Taraori in Karnal district, Haryana. Addressing millions of farmers, agricultural scientists and officials who joined virtually from Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and agricultural institutions across the country, Shri Chouhan warned that unless the unbalanced use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides was brought under control, the earth could eventually refuse to produce crops and the human body could become a breeding ground for diseases. On the occasion, he called for a comprehensive public awareness campaign in every village across the country from 22nd October to 30th November 2026. As Rural Development Minister, he also announced a major benefit for poor families in Haryana. He handed over to Haryana Agriculture Minister Shri Shyam Singh Rana, on behalf of the state government, an approval letter for financial assistance of ₹1,343.06 crore to construct 28,422 permanent houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin.

Haryana’s farmers have shown the way forward for the entire country

Addressing a large farmers’ convention held on the historic land of Taraori, Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that Haryana’s farmers were remarkable for their hard work, dedication and willingness to experiment with new approaches. He observed that progressive farmers from Haryana were writing a new chapter of agricultural transformation not only in their own state but also in states such as Madhya Pradesh, where they were promoting modern and natural farming practices. Emphasising Haryana’s influence on agricultural progress across the country, he said that when Haryana showed the way, the entire nation moved forward in that direction. He added that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, too, felt deeply concerned about the deteriorating health of Mother Earth and the need to improve the condition of the country’s agricultural land.

Major benefit for Haryana under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana

During the programme, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, in his capacity as Union Rural Development Minister, made a major announcement for rural poor families in Haryana. He said that the central government had approved the construction of 28,422 permanent houses for eligible poor families in the state under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. An amount of ₹1,343 crore and ₹6 lakh had been sanctioned for this purpose. Shri Chouhan handed over the formal approval letter for this significant allocation to Haryana Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Minister Shri Shyam Singh Rana, who was present on the stage. The approval is expected to help thousands of economically disadvantaged families in the state realise their dream of owning a permanent home.

Affordable fertilisers do not mean indiscriminate use; the government is bearing the subsidy burden

Speaking about fertiliser prices and the government’s commitment to farmers, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that despite rising prices in international markets, the central government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, was ensuring that farmers did not face any additional financial burden. The government was bearing a substantial fertiliser subsidy of more than ₹1.5 lakh crore to ensure that farmers could continue to obtain a bag of urea for just ₹266 and a bag of DAP for ₹1,350. However, he cautioned farmers against assuming that the availability of affordable fertilisers justified their excessive use. “Getting fertilisers at affordable prices certainly does not mean that we should keep applying four bags of urea to our fields. It is a misconception that applying more fertiliser will produce a bigger harvest. Applying fertilisers without need is like wasting our hard-earned money and poisoning the soil. Just as a person can become ill by taking medicines without being sick, excessive fertiliser use is making the health of our Mother Earth deteriorate,” he said. He added that India was now moving towards the use of green ammonia, which would help the country become fully self-reliant (atmanirbhar) in fertiliser production in the future.

Pesticides are turning the human body into a breeding ground for diseases; both people and fields must be protected

Highlighting the serious consequences of chemical-intensive farming, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that consuming food produced with poisonous pesticides and excessive, uncontrolled fertiliser use was increasingly turning the human body into a breeding ground for serious diseases. He observed that air, water and food were essential for human survival, and that ancient scriptures regarded food as Brahma, or the divine. If the food itself became impure, he warned, the very existence of human civilisation could be threatened. He stressed that the present effort was not merely a struggle to protect soil but a sacred mission to safeguard both agricultural land and human life. Protecting the health of the fields, he emphasised, was inseparable from protecting the health of the people who depended on them.

Three practical principles for soil conservation

Union Minister Shri Chouhan outlined three key measures that farmers could adopt to preserve soil fertility and maintain productive agricultural land.

Balanced fertiliser use based on Soil Health Cards: Farmers should check their Soil Health Cards on their mobile phones and identify which nutrients are deficient in their soil. They should then apply only the required fertilisers, in balanced quantities, to address those deficiencies rather than using fertilisers indiscriminately.

Changing the crop cycle through crop rotation: Instead of repeatedly growing paddy followed by wheat, farmers should introduce pulses such as chickpea, lentil and pigeon pea into their cropping cycles. The roots of pulse crops naturally fix nitrogen in the soil, helping to improve its fertility and replenish nutrients.

Adopting natural farming on at least half an acre: Farmers need not initially convert their entire landholding to natural farming. Even if they have five acres, they should begin by adopting natural farming on at least half an acre. They can prepare Beejamrit and Ghanjeevamrit using cow dung, cow urine and soil collected from beneath trees. This would provide chemical-free food for household consumption, reduce cultivation costs and improve soil health. Over two to three years, soil conditions would improve and production could reach levels comparable to those achieved through conventional farming.

Crop-residue management and protection of earthworms, the soil’s natural allies

Appreciating the efforts of Taraori’s farmers to manage crop residue and maintain high levels of organic carbon in their soil, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that burning crop residue was a self-destructive practice. He explained that setting fire to fields not only causes air pollution but also destroys trillions of microorganisms living in the upper and lower layers of the soil, along with beneficial insects and earthworms that help produce natural manure. These organisms play an essential role in maintaining the soil’s natural fertility. Protecting earthworms and beneficial insects, he stressed, was therefore crucial to preserving the health and productivity of agricultural land.

Nationwide public awareness campaign to run from 22nd October to 30th November, 2026

Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan called upon vice-chancellors of agricultural universities, the Director General of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), scientists and officials to leave their laboratories and offices and visit villages across the country from 22nd October to 30th November, 2026. They should organise village-level meetings and discussions with farmers to explain the importance of soil health and balanced farming practices. He expressed his resolve to remain actively involved in the campaign on the ground himself, ensuring that the initiative reached farmers directly and helped protect India’s agricultural land from becoming barren.

Farmers raise their hands and pledge to protect their fields

At the conclusion of his address, responding to Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s appeal, the farmers gathered at the venue raised both hands, clenched their fists and took a collective pledge amid resounding slogans of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai”. They resolved to use chemicals in their fields in a balanced manner, change their crop cycles, refrain from burning crop residue and gradually adopt natural farming practices to protect the health of Mother Earth.

The historic launch was attended by several prominent agricultural scientists and administrative officials, including ICAR Director General and Secretary of the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) Dr Mangi Lal Jat and Haryana Additional Chief Secretary (Agriculture) Shri Vijendra Kumar, along with a large number of farmers. During the programme, the dignitaries also released a booklet on the ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’.

2326896.title: IICA signs MoU with Association of ARCs in India to strengthen industry linkages with its flagship programme
2326896.body_html:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
IICA signs MoU with Association of ARCs in India to strengthen industry linkages with its flagship programme
Collaboration will cover industry faculty, joint research on distressed assets, data sharing, placement support and an annual joint conference
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 8:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Association of ARCs in India. The Association is the representative body of Asset Reconstruction Companies registered with the Reserve Bank of India. The MoU was signed under the august presence of Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh. Director General & CEO, IICA, by Shri Amrinder Puri, Chief Administrative Officer, IICA and Shri Hari Hara Mishra, Chief Executive Officer, Association of ARCs in India.

The MoU aims to deepen industry linkages of the Post Graduate Insolvency Programme (PGIP), run by IICA’s Centre for Insolvency and Bankruptcy. The PGIP develops a skilled cadre of Insolvency Professionals and Turnaround Specialists. The MoU captures the strategic alignment as decided in the meeting convened by Ministry of Corporate Affairs on 2nd  September 2026.

Delivering the keynote address on the occasion, Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, DG &CEO IICA informed the role of Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs) in the insolvency resolution ecosystem, including their eligibility and participation as resolution applicants under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). He highlighted that the significant development in the evolution of ARCs came on 11 October 2022, when the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), following the recommendations of the Sudarshan Sen Committee, issued its regulatory framework titled Review of Regulatory Framework for Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs) (RBI/2022-23/128). The framework permitted eligible ARCs to act as resolution applicants under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC), subject to the prescribed regulatory conditions.

This development expanded the potential role of ARCs in corporate insolvency resolution, enabling them to participate in resolution processes and contribute their expertise in asset valuation, debt restructuring and the management of stressed assets. It also underscored the importance of transparency, operational efficiency and effective value realisation in the resolution of distressed businesses.

Speaking on behalf ARCs, Shri Hari Hara Mishra, CEO ARC India mentioned that this is an emerging partnership with extraordinary potential. As distressed market evolves, a repository of talent pool and research insights are critical for value maximisation for all stakeholders in the ecosystem. He desired that implementation strategy should be immediately put in place in achieving the overall objectives in general and transforming the academic rigour of PGIP course in particular.

The proposed collaboration is expected to strengthen the integration of theoretical knowledge with practical industry experience, preparing PGIP participants to respond more effectively to the complexities of insolvency resolution, corporate restructuring and financial distress management. The MoU establishes a collaborative framework built around three key pillars:

1. Industry-oriented curriculum and capacity building: Industry experts from ARCs will contribute to teaching, faculty support to reorient PGIP course modules more industry-oriented and responsive to emerging professional requirements.

2. Research, data sharing and knowledge creation: The collaboration will promote joint research projects in areas such as debt restructuring, financial markets, stressed assets and insolvency resolution. Data sharing, subject to applicable legal, regulatory, confidentiality and access requirements, will support evidence-based research and the development of research resources on market trends and developments.

3. Joint programmes and industry engagement: The two institutions will explore internships, placement- related opportunities and greater industry interaction for PGIP participants. An annual joint conference will provide a platform for discussing emerging challenges, sharing professional insights and disseminating research findings.

Looking Ahead

The MoU, signed for a period of five years, provides a structured framework for sustained engagement between IICA and the Association of ARCs. The institutions will work towards translating the agreement into tangible outcomes through defined implementation strategies, collaborative research, expert-led teaching and regular review of progress.

The discussions also explored the possibility of organising a joint conference in February 2027 around the milestones of IBC@10 and SARFAESI@25, with the theme and programme to be finalised jointly within the broad spectrum of activities enunciated in the MoU.

2326901.title: 8 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Underway
2326901.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
8 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Underway
Hundreds of Visitors Throng Mela At Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati
Mela Promotes Market Access, Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Livelihoods for Artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs).
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 8:24PM by PIB Delhi

The 08 days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 is underway at Guwahati, the State Capital of Assam. The Mela is being organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, until October 28 Wednesday.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela is open to public at Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati, from 11 A.M. onwards till 9 O’ Clock. He said the visitors are exploring the diverse range of traditional products to purchase the creations and support the artisans.

He said the Mela is bringing together artisans from across the country, including the North-Eastern States, to showcase India’s rich and diverse heritage of traditional handicrafts and handloom products.

The Official said a total of 75 artisans, including 31 women artisans, are participating in the Mela, displaying approximately 40 varieties of handloom and handicraft products.

He said the event is providing participating artisans with a platform to exhibit and sell their products directly to visitors, establish connections with prospective customers and explore opportunities to expand their market reach.

By facilitating direct interaction between artisans and consumers, the Mela seeks to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and improve livelihood opportunities for participating artisans, he added.


The Official said the Guwahati edition features a wide range of traditional crafts and handloom products representing different regions of India.

 

The participation of artisans from the North-Eastern States, alongside those from other parts of the country, will provide visitors with an opportunity to appreciate the diversity of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and cultural heritage, he added.

 

 

He said the event aims to also encourage greater appreciation of the skills and creativity of artisans whose work contributes to preserving traditional knowledge and craft practices.

The Official further said a key focus of the Mela is the promotion of BHARAT-TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme), an initiative aimed at facilitating the marketing of products made by artisans belonging to the target groups through physical outlets and e-commerce platforms.

 

By promoting access to wider markets and digital channels, the initiative is aimed to strengthen market linkages, expand customer outreach and create additional opportunities for artisans to enhance their earnings.

 

It also supports the preservation and promotion of traditional arts and crafts by connecting artisans and their products with evolving consumer markets, he said.

 

The Shilp Samagam Mela (SSM-2026) is an important initiative of the Ministry to provide marketing support to artisans and beneficiaries associated with its three National Corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), and the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC).

 

 

The first edition of SSM 2026 concluded in Mysuru on October 19, with thousands of visitors thronging the nine days Mela at Dasara Exhibition Ground, Mysuru in Karnataka.

 

Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s principle of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas”, the Mela is promotiong the economic empowerment of artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs).

 

The Mela is providing a dedicated platform for these communities to showcase their skills, market their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance through sustainable livelihood opportunities.

In addition to promoting the sale of traditional products, the Mela is creating awareness among visitors and participating communities about the welfare, financial assistance and development schemes implemented by the Ministry and its three National Corporations.

 

 

The initiative is complementing financial and developmental support with market-oriented interventions, enabling artisans to translate their traditional skills and craftsmanship into viable livelihood opportunities, the official said.

It is pertinent to mention that through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to advance its efforts towards the socio-economic empowerment of communities having financial constraints, by promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating market access and supporting sustainable livelihoods.

The Mela is enhancing the visibility of participating artisans, expanding awareness of their products and encouraging greater public engagement with India’s rich handloom and handicraft traditions.

2326852.title: Union Secretary MoSJ&E Shri Sudhansh Pant Lauds J&K’s Grassroots Welfare Outreach, Whole-Of-Government Approach Against Drug Abuse
2326852.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Secretary MoSJ&E Shri Sudhansh Pant Lauds J&K’s Grassroots Welfare Outreach, Whole-Of-Government Approach Against Drug Abuse
J&K Chief Secretary Shri Atal Dulloo Reiterates Commitment To Saturation Of Welfare Schemes
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:45PM by PIB Delhi

Union Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Sudhansh Pant, today lauded Jammu and Kashmir’s extensive grassroots outreach under social welfare schemes and its coordinated, whole-of government approach to combating drug abuse, describing the UT’s efforts as a commendable model with potential for replication across the country.

Shri Pant made these observations during a comprehensive review of the implementation of various social welfare schemes and programmes in Jammu and Kashmir, chaired jointly by him and Chief Secretary, Atal Dulloo.

The meeting was attended by Additional Chief Secretary, Home; Commissioner Secretary, Education; Secretary, Social Welfare Department; Secretary, Health; Director General, Social Welfare, Kashmir; Director, Social Welfare, Jammu; Head of Department, Psychiatry, Government Medical College, Srinagar; Secretary, SC/ST/OBC Boards, besides officers of other concerned departments.

Appreciating the UT Administration’s efforts to extend welfare interventions to the grassroots, the Union Secretary observed that the outreach undertaken across villages and panchayats reflected a strong commitment to inclusive welfare delivery. He particularly commended J&K’s coordinated campaign against the drug menace, noting that its whole-of-government approach had received nationwide appreciation and could serve as a successful model for other regions.

Expressing satisfaction over the progress of individual beneficiary-oriented schemes, the Union Secretary highlighted the importance of ensuring that interventions for students, senior citizens, destitute women and other vulnerable sections deliver meaningful outcomes. He advised the Administration to document first-hand beneficiary testimonies and showcase the thousands of success stories emerging from these initiatives to generate wider awareness and amplify their impact across the country.

Reviewing the rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging, Shri Pant encouraged the UT Administration to work towards achieving the ‘Begging-Free City’ status for its urban centres. He observed that the relatively small number of such persons could be addressed through focused rehabilitation, sustained support and collaboration with dedicated non-governmental organisations.

The Union Secretary also outlined key priorities and focus areas for the UT to facilitate the achievement of the Ministry’s objectives. He appreciated Chief Secretary Atal Dulloo for his continued guidance and mentoring of the J&K's Social Welfare Department, observing that its diverse mandate required close coordination across multiple departments for effective implementation.

Speaking on the occasion, Chief Secretary Atal Dulloo reaffirmed the Government’s unwavering commitment to inclusive growth, social justice and community empowerment. He emphasized that the UT Administration was committed to saturating the benefits of welfare schemes among all eligible and deserving beneficiaries, particularly those belonging to disadvantaged and underprivileged sections of society.

Further the Chief Secretary threw light on the population profile of various beneficiary groups in J&K, the welfare measures available for their upliftment and the legal, institutional and regulatory safeguards established to protect their rights and prevent atrocities, discrimination and harassment. He stressed the importance of coordinated efforts to ensure that the benefits of these interventions reach every eligible beneficiary.

On this occasion the Secretary, Social Welfare Department, Doifode Sagar Dattatray, presented a detailed appraisal of the progress achieved under various centrally sponsored and UT-level schemes, covering drug demand reduction, educational scholarships, senior citizen welfare, rehabilitation, sanitation-worker safety, community development and legal protection for vulnerable groups.

Under the Nasha Mukt J&K 100 Days Abhiyan, the Department reported extensive public outreach through coordinated efforts involving multiple departments. It was revealed that more than 7.21 million outreach events had been conducted across the UT with Addiction Treatment Facilities handling 66,594 outpatients, while the Department’s Drug De-addiction and Rehabilitation Centres providing care to 1,053 individuals.

On the enforcement front, it was given out that the Police had registered 1,187 FIRs and arrested 1,349 persons. With respect to financial investigations the meeting was apprised that the same resulted in the seizure or attachment of 125 immovable properties valued at ₹9,828.17 lakh and 60 movable assets worth ₹703.83 lakh belonging to drug traffickers. The meeting was informed that the proposed Rehabilitation and Socio-Economic Reintegration Scheme for Drug Abuse Victims, 2026, envisaging a structured three-year recovery framework.

On this occasion, Dr Arshad Hussain, Head of the Department of Psychiatry, GMC Srinagar, elaborated on J&K’s ‘Circle of Care’ approach to addressing substance use disorders. The three-dimensional strategy provides continuity of care from admission to de-addiction facilities through treatment, rehabilitation, social reintegration and long-term monitoring to support sustained recovery.

Moreover it was divulged that under the Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana, it was informed that 419 villages had been selected for development as model villages, of which 28 had been declared Adarsh Grams. A total of 81 development works had been completed during 2026–27 so far. The meeting also reviewed the funding requirement for completing subsequent phases of the programme.

The Department informed that ₹496.59 lakh had been utilised under the Grants in-Aid component of PM-AJAY towards basic infrastructure, skill development and income-generating assets. Similarly under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana, 17 Senior Citizen Homes were operational across the UT, including eight in Jammu division, accommodating around 450 senior citizens, and nine in Kashmir division.

 

The review also covered educational scholarships under PM-YASASVI for OBC, EBC and DNT communities and scholarship schemes for Scheduled Caste students. As of October 15, 2026, a total of 20,611 applications had been received against a target of 24,817 under PM-YASASVI for the academic year 2026–27.

Under the Scheduled Caste scholarship schemes, 5,613 post-matric and 2,866 pre matric applications had been submitted through the National Scholarship Portal. Special drives and individual follow-ups were underway to clear pending cases and expedite Aadhaar seeding.

Under the National Action for Mechanized Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE), 741 sewer and septic tank workers had been profiled across 74 Urban Local Bodies, of whom 734 had been validated. In addition, 5,862 urban waste pickers had been profiled, with 4,508 validated. The Department had distributed 721 personal protective equipment kits to sewer and septic tank workers and 3,854 kits to waste pickers.

The meeting reviewed the implementation of safeguards under the Protection of Civil Rights framework and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. In this direction the SAMBAL 2.0 portal had resolved 63 of the 66 online grievances registered. Relief amounting to ₹58.60 lakh had been disbursed through direct benefit transfers to 50 victims of atrocities between 2022 and 2026.

During the deliberations, J&K highlighted the pending central financial share for certain OBC hostel projects had affected their completion. The UT Administration sought the Ministry’s intervention for the release of the requisite funds to facilitate early completion of these facilities.

The review emphasised the need for sustained interdepartmental coordination, effective beneficiary outreach, timely resolution of implementation bottlenecks and a stronger focus on documenting and publicising success stories to ensure that welfare interventions translate into tangible improvements in the lives of people across Jammu and Kashmir.

2326841.title: Tripartite MoU signed to strengthen livelihood opportunities for Scheduled Tribe youth
2326841.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Tripartite MoU signed to strengthen livelihood opportunities for Scheduled Tribe youth
Livelihood Business Incubation Centre at Rourkela has benefited more than 600 students
Centre recognised as a Centre of Excellence by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, through the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC), is supporting livelihood promotion and entrepreneurship development for Scheduled Tribe (ST) youth through the Livelihood Business Incubation Centre at Rourkela, Odisha. A Tripartite MoU was signed on 22.10.2026 between National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation under Ministry of Tribal Affairs, National Skill Development Corporation (NSIC) under Ministry of Medium and Small-Scale Industries (MSME), and Steel Authority of India Ltd. – Rourkela Steel Plant (RSP, Rourkela) under Ministry of Steel.


 

Focus on skill development and sustainable livelihoods:

Economic empowerment of a community can be made more effective only when there is a special focus to upgrade their skills and processes through providing of the required skills. Enrichment of skills and knowledge has to be intricately linked with the funding structure to facilitate creation of sustainable livelihood systems among the STs. Capacity building in specific job roles and imparting basic knowledge on financial aspects of marketing, branding are vital requirement for budding entrepreneurs.

Livelihood Business Incubation Centre at Rourkela:

Livelihood Incubation Centre at Rourkela, Odisha was established in 2018 which has been recognized as Center of Excellence by Ministry of Tribal Affairs is one such major step. This is a unique collaborative effort of three Ministries of Government of India and three Central level Apex PSUs under them namely, National Skill Development Corporation (NSIC) under Ministry of Medium and Small scale Industries (MSME), Steel Authority of India Ltd. - Rourkela Steel Plant (RSP, Rourkela) under Ministry of Steel and National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation under Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

Training and entrepreneurship development:

The basic objective of the center is to provide training, skill development and entrepreneurship development programmes to local ST youths to promote sustainable enterprises. The idea is to raise confidence, improve productivity and give direction through proper livelihood creation by the synergy of training, and hand holding.

Courses covered for the students from ST community in the current year are Assistant Beautician, Self Employed Tailor, Assistant Computer Operator (Tally & Accounting), Assistant Electrician, Bread & Bakery Manufacturing, Mushroom Farming. Accordingly, the site is to be provided by Rourkela Steel Plant, Plant and Machinery are installed under ASPIRE scheme of MSME and recurring expenses of the center is being borne by NSTFDC through grant from Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

The Centre offered training in various courses viz. Welding Technology, Furniture Manufacturing, Soya Milk extraction, Tofu Packaging, Beautician, Manufacturing Trade (Bread & Bakery) courses. The centre is creating awareness amongst the prospective trainees. More than 600 students had benefited from the Centre and had set up their own business activities in the various trades like bakery, mushroom cultivation, beauty parlour, tailoring etc.

Officials present at the event:

Sh. T. Roumuan Paite, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs and CMD NSTFDC graced the event along-with Sh. Kunj Bihari, Company Secretary, Ms. Bismita Das, AGM (Projects & CSR) and Sh. Sunil Sahoo, Chief Zonal Manager, East Zone.

Sh. Tapankumar G. Kanekar, CGM (TS & CSR) and Sh. R.S. Bora DGM (CSR) on behalf of SAIL and Sh. O.P. Singh, Sr. General Manager (Tech. Training & Development Vertical & SBU Head) and Sh. Markandey Kumar, Chief Manager on behalf of NSIC were present in the event.

Discussion on the functioning of the Centre:

There was an interactive session with the trainees, faculties and meeting with NSIC officials to discuss various issues pertaining to functioning of the Center. Way forward strategies regarding mobilization of candidates, working of current modules and other issues relating to progress of trainees were discussed.

2326836.title: 1, 87,305 Candidates Trained and Placed 96,162 During 2020-21 to 2023-24 under PM-DAKSH Scheme
2326836.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
1, 87,305 Candidates Trained and Placed 96,162 During 2020-21 to 2023-24 under PM-DAKSH Scheme
From 2024-25 onwards, PM-DAKSH Merged with PMKVY Scheme of MSDE
Evaluation Study Reports Over 90% of Beneficiaries Found Training Aligned with Career Goals and Local Labour Market Needs
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Pradhan Mantri Dakshata Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH), a Central Sector Scheme, was launched during 2020-21 to provide skill training to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), De-notified Tribes (DNTs), and Safai Karamcharis, including Waste Pickers, through empanelled training institutes to encourage self-employment and wage-employment for their socio-economic development.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the scheme was implemented by three Corporations of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE), namely, the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

The Official said that from 2024-25 onwards, it was decided to merge PM-DAKSH with the PMKVY Scheme of MSDE. As PM-DAKSH was an additionality to PMKVY and all job roles for providing skill training were taken from the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) portal, which were also covered under PMKVY, PM-DAKSH was subsumed under PMKVY to avoid duplication, she added.

The Official said the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment releases funds to the Corporations, which reimburse training costs to institutes empanelled under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), as per the scheme guidelines and work order.

She said after training completion, institutes are required to provide wage-employment and/or self-employment to at least 70% of trained candidates. If this requirement is not met, the third instalment, amounting to 30% of the training cost, is forfeited. Training institutes are also mandated to maintain collaboration with relevant industries to facilitate employment opportunities for trained candidates. The three Corporations extend loan facilities and assistance to eligible youth from the target group in setting up their projects by providing handholding support, the Official added.

Against the total funds allotted for PM-DAKSH from 2020-21 to 2023-24 amounting to ₹276.47 crore, actual expenditure of ₹309.5 crore had been incurred till date. During 2020-21 to 2023-24, 1,87,305 candidates were trained and 96,162 candidates were placed, the Official said.

The Official further said the evaluation study of the PM-DAKSH Scheme shows strong relevance and learning effectiveness, with over 90% of beneficiaries reporting alignment of training with their career goals and local labour market needs, as well as achievement of intended learning outcomes. Impact results indicate non-material gains such as improved confidence, self-esteem and social recognition, particularly among women and marginalised groups. Sustainability outcomes are largely positive, with most beneficiaries continuing to use the skills acquired, expecting long-term income growth, reinvesting in development and feeling capable of maintaining improvements independently, the Official added.

2326832.title: AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026
2326832.ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
2326832.body_html:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026
Day 2 Highlights State Leadership, Next-Gen Technology, and Blended Finance Mechanisms
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:26PM by PIB Delhi

The second day of the AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026 accelerated cross-sectoral engagement across state policy leadership, technological innovation, private sector engagement and climate finance solutions.

A dedicated ministerial track, co-organised by the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) and the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW), brought together State Ministers of Energy and Agriculture from Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Bihar to present state-level approaches for accelerating agrivoltaic deployment. The session served as a platform for states to showcase investment opportunities, highlighting innovative land-use models, state-level tariff incentives, and adaptation of the PM-KUSUM scheme to local agricultural conditions and crop profiles. Discussions underscored the growing role of sub-national governments in creating enabling environments for agrivoltaic investments.

Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma, Minister of Energy, Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the state’s vast agricultural base, diverse cropping patterns and expanding solar infrastructure as key advantages for agrivoltaics. He emphasised that generating solar power alongside cultivation would optimise land use and create an additional income stream for farmers. Highlighting Uttar Pradesh’s progress in rooftop solar and grid infrastructure, he noted that Green Energy Corridor-III would further strengthen power evacuation for renewable energy projects. He also stressed the need for financing models and technologies suited to small and marginal farmers, who account for nearly 80% of agricultural holdings in the state. Inviting investors to explore these opportunities, he said, “The potential for agrivoltaics is enormous. Those who wish to be associated with agrivoltaics need to look towards Uttar Pradesh.” He also assured investors of the state’s support for grid connectivity and power evacuation.

Shri Surya Pratap Shahi, Minister of Agriculture, Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the state’s plan to solarise all 16 lakh agricultural tubewells whose electricity bills have been waived, supported by dedicated grid infrastructure. He emphasised that farmers’ land ownership rights must be protected and called for structured training on crop selection and agrivoltaic practices. He proposed leveraging Krishi Vigyan Kendras, agricultural universities and technical institutions to build farmers’ capacity, while integrating agrivoltaics with agricultural diversification and existing farmer-support initiatives. Highlighting the central role of farmers in the state’s economy, he said, “The agriculture of Uttar Pradesh and its farmers are, in a way, the lifeblood of our economic system.” He also assured farmers that ownership of their land would remain protected.

Shri Rakesh Shukla, Minister of New and Renewable Energy, Madhya Pradesh, highlighted the state’s efforts to advance agrivoltaics, solar deployment and battery storage as part of its farmer-welfare agenda, with 2026 being observed as the Year of Farmer Welfare in Madhya Pradesh. He noted that cultivation beneath solar panels had begun at several locations and that the state was progressing with battery-storage projects, for which the tendering process had been completed. He also highlighted Madhya Pradesh’s wider renewable energy infrastructure, including the Omkareshwar project. Emphasising the state’s progress in agrivoltaics, he said, “In the agricultural sector, we have some plants where farming takes place beneath solar panels. Such projects have begun at a few locations in Madhya Pradesh, and we are continuously progressing in this direction, including in battery storage, for which we have also completed the tendering process.”

Shri Shailesh Kumar Mandal, Minister of Energy, Bihar, highlighted the state’s efforts to strengthen agricultural electricity infrastructure through feeder separation and solarisation. He noted that Bihar had advanced work on approximately 2,700 agricultural feeders, with the state government approving financial support for their solarisation. Emphasising Bihar’s longstanding familiarity with solar energy and its commitment to expanding renewable energy access, he said, “Solar energy and sunlight are not new concepts in Bihar; this tradition has existed there for centuries.” He reiterated the state government’s commitment to taking forward agricultural feeder solarisation through an innovative approach.

Shri Vijay Kumar Sinha, Minister of Agriculture, Bihar, highlighted agrivoltaics as an opportunity to enhance farmers’ incomes, promote crop diversification and generate rural employment. He emphasised the need to strengthen research, farmer awareness and training through collaboration among agricultural institutions, financial institutions and energy enterprises. He also highlighted Bihar’s contribution to the country’s workforce as an opportunity to support wider adoption and implementation of agrivoltaics. He said, “A large pool of workers comes from Bihar and contributes to the workforce across the country. Many states rely on this workforce from Bihar.”

Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo, Deputy Chief Minister, Odisha, announced that the state is finalising its dedicated Agrivoltaics Policy 2026, with a target of 1 GW by 2030. The proposed policy will require at least 90% of project sites to remain cultivable, safeguard farmer consent and crop insurance, and allow farmers to own projects or lease their land while continuing cultivation. To attract investment, Odisha plans to provide 25-year power purchase agreements through GRIDCO, grid connectivity and investment incentives. Highlighting the policy’s importance for investors, he said, “It gives investors certainty: 25 years of PPA with GRIDCO, an offtake guarantee, grid connectivity and the freedom of open access and competitive use.” He also announced that Odisha is finalising its dedicated Agrivoltaics Policy 2026, positioning the state to establish a policy framework specifically for agrivoltaics.

 The Agrivoltaics Pitch-Hub was curated by the National Solar Energy Federation of India (NSEFI) where early-stage innovators and start-ups pitched bankable, dual-use agrivoltaic solutions before an expert jury comprising national institutes (NISE, NIBE), venture capitalists, and industry leaders.

Fraunhofer ISE and Sunseed APV demonstrated next-generation solutions, including advanced solar tracking systems, dynamic panel tilting, semi-transparent photovoltaic (PV) modules, and micro-climate soil sensors engineered specifically for tropical and arid conditions.

Hosted by the Indo-German Chamber of Commerce, the dialogue brought together Indian and international developers, including NTPC Green Energy, First Solar, and leading European firms to discuss supply chain localisation, standards development, and market certainty.

An executive roundtable convened representatives from multilateral development banks, financial institutions, and commercial lenders, including the World Bank, KfW, European Investment Bank, and IREDA.

Participants examined financial mechanisms needed to accelerate agrivoltaic deployment, including risk-mitigation instruments, concessional lending facilities, and blended finance structures capable of mobilising private investment at scale.

Bringing a vital youth perspective to the global stage, acclaimed actress and UNDP India Youth Champion Sanjana Sanghi joined the Conference for an exclusive fireside chat. Sanghi advocated for youth-led community strategies and spotlighted the intersection of food security, renewable energy, and youth mobilisation. She emphasised how agrivoltaics contributes to multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) while directly empowering and securing livelihoods for rural youth.

The day concluded with an interactive Digital Poster Gallery, showcasing operational agrivoltaic projects and lessons from global case studies, providing participants with practical insights into implementation and scale-up strategies.

2326831.title: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal Invites Polish Firms to ‘Build, Innovate and Grow with India’
2326831.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2326831.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal Invites Polish Firms to ‘Build, Innovate and Grow with India’
Sonowal proposes Startup Bridge, Innovation Corridor & AI-Quantum Dialogue to link India and Poland
At “India-Poland Business Forum” with PM Donald Tusk, Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal offers “India's Scale, Skills & Trust for Joint Growth”
Sonowal pitches India's growth story to Polish business leaders calls for “trusted supply chains”
Let us invest, innovate and develop together: Sonowal at India-Poland Business Forum
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW) Sarbananda Sonowal urged Polish companies to “build, innovate and invest in India” rather than only sell to it, as he pitched the country's growth story to business leaders from both nations.

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal delivered the keynote address at the India-Poland Business Forum here today which was also attended by Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Sonowal recalled that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Poland in August 2024 lifted ties to a strategic partnership.

“When Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Poland in August 2024, he and Prime Minister Tusk elevated our relations to a Strategic Partnership. They did so with a clear conviction: the India-Poland relationship must not only be strong in diplomacy; it must also be strong in business, technology, investment and innovation,” said Sarbananda Sonowal. The aim now, he said, is for the relationship to be as strong in business, technology, investment and innovation as it is in diplomacy.

"India offers the scale of a large and growing market, the skills of a young and talented workforce, and the trust of a democracy committed to reform, enterprise and openness," Sonowal said.

Sonowal argued that the two economies fit together. Poland, he said, has strengths in engineering, machinery, mining technologies, transport, environmental solutions and advanced manufacturing. India has the market, talent and manufacturing base to give those capabilities scale. "My message to Polish companies is: do not only sell to India. Build in India. Develop solutions in India. Find Indian partners. And, use India as a platform for growth," Sonowal said.

Sonowal cited that India, under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has set an ambitious target to generate 500 GW of non-fossil fuel power capacity by 2030, to put forth a strong Climate Action step by the country. He put the investment needed at roughly 280 billion to 300 billion euros, with openings for equipment makers, storage, power grids, green hydrogen, recycling and environmental technology. Poland's experience in mining, critical minerals and clean energy could help, Sonowal said.

On technology, Sonowal noted that Indian IT companies have made Poland a base for their European operations and employ about 10,000 people there. He said the next step should go beyond IT services, into artificial intelligence, quantum computing, 5G applications, digital infrastructure, smart manufacturing and space.

The Union Minister proposed a Startup Bridge, an Innovation Corridor and an AI and Quantum Dialogue to link businesses, researchers and innovators in both countries. Trade between the two countries has reached $6.36 billion, and Indian investment in Poland exceeds $3 billion, Sonowal said. Polish companies are also active in India in packaging, manufacturing, waste-to-energy and electric mobility. He said the ambition should be larger than doubling trade by 2030.

"We should create together. We should innovate together. We should invest together. We should build trusted supply chains together. And we should succeed together," Sonowal said.

He urged business leaders to see the India-EU free trade agreement as more than a trade pact. "View it as a partnership multiplier," he said. It opens a larger window into the Indian market for Polish firms, he said, and widens European opportunities for Indian ones.

Sonowal concluded by describing India’s philosophy of “Power to Empower”, stating that beyond the power to compete lies the power to collaborate. “India’s growth can create opportunities for Poland. Poland’s capabilities can add strength to India. And together, our businesses can create solutions for the world,” he said.

2326828.title: CAQM Reviews Air Pollution Control Measures in Punjab and Haryana, Calls for Prompt Ground-Level Action
2326828.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2326828.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM Reviews Air Pollution Control Measures in Punjab and Haryana, Calls for Prompt Ground-Level Action
Focus on prevention of Paddy Stubble Burning, effective utilization of CRM Machinery, stronger Enforcement and control of other key Pollution Sources
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM, held separate review meetings with the Governments of Punjab and Haryana in Chandigarh today to review the measures being undertaken for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning and abatement of other key sources of air pollution, calling for prompt action(s) on the ground.

The meeting with the Government of Punjab focused on implementation of the State Action Plan for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning in accordance with CAQM Direction No. 99 dated 15.05.2026. The Commission reviewed on-ground enforcement measures, District-level preparedness and monitoring mechanisms in place for effective paddy stubble management.

The availability, deployment and effective utilization of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery at the District and farmer levels were reviewed, along with the identification of gaps in machinery utilization and arrangements for the collection, transportation and utilization of paddy straw through in-situ and ex-situ management. The Commission emphasized the need to strengthen the crop-residue supply chain and ensure effective utilization of available machinery during the peak harvesting period.

The meeting also covered field validation of burnt-area assessment through satellite-based fire alerts, along with District-wise deployment of drones and low-cost sensors for monitoring stubble-burning incidents. Compliance with CAQM Direction No. 92, mandating the use of paddy straw-based biomass pellets/ briquettes in brick kilns, and progress towards prescribed targets for biomass co-firing in thermal power plants were also reviewed.

The meeting with the Government of Haryana covered a broader range of air pollution sources, including paddy stubble burning, abatement of vehicular pollution, dust from roads and open areas, dust from construction and demolition (C&D) activities and industrial pollution, along with other identified sectoral measures.

With regard to paddy stubble burning, the Commission reviewed implementation of the State Action Plan, including on-ground enforcement, deployment and utilization of CRM machinery, crop-residue supply-chain management, field validation of burnt-area assessment and the use of drones and low-cost sensors for monitoring burning incidents. Compliance with Direction No. 92 regarding biomass pellets/ briquettes in brick kilns and progress on biomass co-firing in thermal power plants were also taken up.

The review of vehicular pollution covered installation of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system at fuel and CNG stations for enforcement of requirements relating to valid Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCCs), action against end-of-life vehicles, adoption of cleaner mobility measures and progress towards phasing out diesel-operated auto rickshaws in NCR Districts.

Measures for dust mitigation from roads and open areas, including road-dust control and mechanized road sweeping, were also reviewed. The Commission further examined measures for controlling dust emissions from C&D activities and implementation of prescribed dust-mitigation measures. The review also covered industrial pollution control, including compliance with applicable norms and monitoring and enforcement measures relating to industrial units and other identified sources.

The Commission emphasized the need for time-bound implementation of State Action Plans, its enforcement and continuous field-level monitoring, supported by close coordination among the concerned State Departments, District Administrations and enforcement agencies. The States were advised to address implementation gaps on priority and ensure timely corrective action across the respective sectors. The Commission emphasized on greater facilitation of farmers with in-situ crop residue management machinery and strengthened ex-situ mechanism. State Governments of Haryana and Punjab were also advised to implement IEC Action Plans on-ground more effectively.

The Commission emphasized that paddy stubble management should be pursued not merely as a measure to prevent burning, but as an opportunity to improve the well-being of citizens while fostering a robust industrial ecosystem of a circular economy, with greater utilization of paddy straw as a resource. The Commission called for prompt action at the ground level and further cautioned the District Administrations that any laxity that leads to rise in stubble-burning incidents shall be viewed seriously.

CAQM reiterated that sustained and coordinated efforts by the State Governments and all concerned agencies are essential for effective prevention of paddy stubble burning and comprehensive abatement of air pollution, particularly during the critical winter period.

2326787.title: At CII conference, Union Environment Minister calls for coordinated efforts by Government, Industry and Urban Local Bodies to advance India’s Circular Economy
2326787.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2326787.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
At CII conference, Union Environment Minister calls for coordinated efforts by Government, Industry and Urban Local Bodies to advance India’s Circular Economy
Government translating Policy Intent into Meaningful Action through Clear Policies and Regulatory Reforms: Shri Bhupender Yadav 
Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today addressed the Circular Economy Conference organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in New Delhi. He highlighted India’s efforts to translate policy intent into meaningful action through clear policies, regulatory reforms, digital compliance systems and a whole-of-government approach to advance the circular economy.

Addressed the @FollowCII Circular Economy Conference in Delhi today. Elaborated on how India under the leadership of Hon'ble PM Shri @narendramodi ji has adopted a 'whole of government' approach in creating an enabling platform for all stakeholders to push circular economy. With clear policy, directions like Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 and EPR framewor, the focus now is on translating policy intent into meaningful action. Happy to note that as of October 12, 2026, more than 86,043 producers and 4,880 recyclers are registered under various EPR frameworks. Through these collective efforts, nearly 499.60 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed across regulated waste streams, with over 435.043 lakh metric tonnes covered through EPR certificate generation.

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) October 22, 2026

In his address, Shri Yadav said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Union Government had progressively strengthened the legal framework governing waste management by introducing sector-specific rules for nine waste streams: plastic waste, battery waste, e-waste, waste tyres, used oil, end-of-life vehicles, construction and demolition waste, non-ferrous scrap metal and solid waste. These rules focused on waste prevention, recycling, reuse, remanufacturing and resource recovery across the product lifecycle. The Minister also highlighted that as on date, nearly 499.60 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed across regulated waste streams, with more than 86,043 producers and 4,880 recyclers registered under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks.  

Highlighting the role of EPR, the Minister said that the framework requires producers, importers and brand owners to ensure environmentally sound management of products at the end of their life. The transfer of EPR certificates provided financial incentives to recyclers, encouraging capacity expansion, technological advancement and increased recycling, while contributing to job creation and livelihoods across the recycling value chain. Shri Yadav emphasised that regulation alone could not create a circular economy and highlighted the importance of Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) initiative, which calls for mindful and deliberate resource utilisation instead of destructive consumption. 

On Industry concerns regarding digital compliance, EPR market operations and transaction timelines, Shri Yadav invited stakeholders to continue sharing practical problems and suggestions. He said the Government is working on a market-based approach and urged industry representatives to engage openly to resolve outstanding issues. On plastic waste management, the Minister called for greater coordination between producers and recyclers to address concerns over the availability of recyclable material and recycling capacity. He said the objective went beyond issuing certificates to creating jobs, strengthening local industry capacity, promoting knowledge-sharing and advancing technology.

While talking about Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, Shri Yadav stressed the need for technology adoption, capacity building, online monitoring, stronger accountability and financial sustainability of urban local bodies. The Minister also highlighted the importance of four-stream segregation of solid waste – wet, dry, sanitary and special-care waste – and public participation. Shri Yadav concluded by emphasising that effective implementation of the SWM Rules would help control legacy waste and strengthen urban systems. He called for coordinated efforts by the government, industry and urban local bodies to advance the circular economy. He further called for stronger recovery of critical minerals from e-waste and batteries, and greater industry participation in developing secondary raw-material markets and strengthening supply-chain traceability.
