2325852.title: DARE/ICAR Undertakes Nearly 4,000 Cleanliness Drives under Swachhata Special Campaign 6.0
2325852.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
DARE/ICAR Undertakes Nearly 4,000 Cleanliness Drives under Swachhata Special Campaign 6.0
Nearly 1.3 Lakh Square Feet of Space Freed under DARE/ICAR’s Swachhata Special Campaign 6.0 
DARE/ICAR Promotes Cleanliness, Waste Management and Sustainable Practices across Its Nationwide Network
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 1:33PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), along with its 114 institutes, Regional Centres, Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes (ATARIs) and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), is participating in the month-long Swachhata Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October 2026.

Earlier, on 2nd October 2026, DARE/ICAR launched Swachhata Special Campaign 6.0 with cleanliness drives across its establishments nationwide. Officials of ICAR Headquarters participated in the drive at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), Pusa, New Delhi. The initiative reflects a collective commitment to cleaner workplaces, greater public participation and a culture of sustained cleanliness, reinforcing the spirit of Swachhata. A floral tribute was also paid to Mahatma Gandhi on his birth anniversary.

Key highlights of Swachhata Special Campaign 6

Key highlights of Swachhata Special Campaign 6 across establishments include the organization of nearly 4,000 cleanliness campaigns, clearance of approximately 1.3 lakh square feet of space, and generation of around ₹10 lakh in revenue through the disposal of electronic and non-electronic scrap. Efforts are also underway to clear pending matters. Activities include cleanliness drives and Shramdaan in institutional premises, villages, roads and public spaces; Special Gram Sabhas, Swachhata Sabhas and awareness programmes on sanitation, hygiene, waste management and community responsibility; plogging and removal of litter; plantation and greening of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs), including initiatives under “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam”; distribution and placement of dustbins; recognition of Safai Mitras, sanitation workers and volunteers; and beautification of cleaned spaces with before-and-after documentation. Other initiatives include sustainable waste management practices, such as vermicomposting of water hyacinth, and the review and weeding out of old files for appropriate disposal and records management.

Key outcomes of the Swachhata Special Campaign 6

The key outcomes of the campaign include strengthened community participation and collective responsibility for cleanliness and sanitation; improved cleanliness of selected institutional and public spaces, documented through before-and-after photographs; and greater awareness of responsible waste disposal through dustbin distribution, waste collection and awareness programmes. The campaign also integrated cleanliness with environmental sustainability through plantation and greening of cleaned areas, recognized the contributions of Safai Mitras, sanitation workers and volunteers, and promoted sustainable practices such as vermicomposting of water hyacinth and the appropriate review and weeding out of old files.

Some of the major highlights of the campaign from DARE/ICAR Institutes are as follows:

ICAR–Central Coastal Agricultural Research Institute : In ICAR–Central Coastal Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR–CCARI), highlight of the occasion was the Shramik Samman, wherein the Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan felicitated Safai Mitras of ICAR–CCARI with shawls, bouquets and gifts, as a mark of appreciation for the dedicated services of all Safai Mitras who work throughout the year to maintain a clean and hygienic campus. The programme highlighted the spirit of Swachhata, Seva and Shramik Samman, recognising the invaluable contribution of Safai Mitras towards a cleaner and healthier environment.

 

                                                                                                                             

ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR-IARI), New Delhi: The ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR-IARI), New Delhi, observed Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2nd October 2026 under the theme “Swachhta Mein Sahbhag – Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”, with a series of cleanliness activities across the Institute and a call for sustained participation towards maintaining a clean and healthy institutional environment. In his address, Secretary (DARE) & DG (ICAR), Dr. Mangi Lal Jat, appreciated the cleanliness drive undertaken by ICAR-IARI and called for making Swachhata a year-round activity, with cleanliness programmes being undertaken in a team-based manner. He emphasised that cleanliness and a better workplace environment contribute to the overall well-being of employees and support the advancement of science and the health of people. The importance of team building and creating a positive workplace environment was highlighted, noting its relevance to both institutional functioning and mental well-being. The importance of nurturing students for their holistic development was emphasized, enabling them to grow as responsible professionals and future contributors to science and society. As part of the programme, prizes were distributed to the winners of the painting competition organised by the Post Graduate School Students’ Union, ICAR-IARI, during the Swachhata Abhiyaan. The competition provided students an opportunity to express their ideas on cleanliness and environmental responsibility through art.

ICAR Institutes and establishments have promoted the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle through activities such as Waste to Art, plastic-free initiatives and creative utilisation of waste materials. Emphasis has also been placed on converting waste into useful and aesthetically meaningful products, promoting awareness on responsible waste management and reinforcing the message that waste can be transformed into a resource.  As part of the cleanliness drive, non-degradable plastic waste, garbage and unwanted weeds were collected and removed from the premises. The activity helped improve the cleanliness and overall appearance of the campus. The participants were also sensitized and made aware of the importance of maintaining a clean and plastic-free campus and encouraged to contribute towards sustainable cleanliness practices.

Under Swachhata Special Campaign 6, DARE/ ICAR are continuously working on raising awareness about hygiene among students for their better health. Our present motto is fostering awareness of civic duties and cultivating corresponding habits for a healthy society. Raising of public awareness and promoting the campaign on a large scale is our goal. Some glimpses at ICAR Research Complex For Eastern Region, Patna, Bihar are shown below.

 

    

ICAR-Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture, Hyderabad, Telangana: in ICAR-CRIDA appearance of the premises are being enhanced along with protection against harmful insects for people visiting or working in the fields. The cleanliness drive is aimed to maintain a clean, hygienic, and environmentally friendly atmosphere within the premises and to create awareness about the importance of cleanliness in agricultural research institutions. Special attention is being given to cleaning the farm surroundings, removing unwanted vegetation, collecting litter and waste materials, and maintaining cleanliness along internal pathways, open spaces, and other common areas. DARE/ ICAR highlights the role of cleanliness in improving workplace efficiency, ensuring the safety of farm personnel, and maintaining the overall appearance of the premises.

          Before Swachhata                                           After Swachhata             

In ICAR-CCARI, Goa, special activity was undertaken for scrap identification from field units to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency by identifying unserviceable and obsolete items for proper disposal. As part of ongoing campaign, a special drive was conducted for the identification of scrap material from guest houses. The scrap like metal items 70 kg, MCB panels 200 kg, fencing wire 100 kg and plastic items 20 kg were identified for disposal. These items were catalogued for further processing under the approved disposal mechanism.

 

  

                                      

Under Special Campaign 6.0, cleanliness and upkeep of the plantation area at ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar, were taken up. The activity covered banana plantation rows and adjoining green spaces, with attention to overgrown weeds, unwanted vegetation and scattered litter. Regular removal of such growth and proper waste disposal are essential to keep plantation areas clean, accessible and well maintained. Key focus was plantation-row maintenance; weed and vegetation management; litter clearance and routine sanitation of institutional green spaces.

 

           ICAR-National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning, Nagpur

 

            

Laboratory waste was collected from various divisions/ sections of the institute and kept in secure location for safe disposal and auction.

 

ICAR-Central Island Agricultural Research Institute

A cleanliness drive was conducted at the Animal Feed Processing Unit of ICAR–CIARI, Sri Vijaya Puram. The activity involved removing accumulated dry leaves, debris, and unwanted vegetation from the roof to maintain cleanliness, ensure proper drainage, and promote regular maintenance of institutional infrastructure under the Swachhata initiative.

 

            Environment-friendly biological waste management activities were undertaken in the cattle, buffalo, goat and pig units of the institute, covering a total of 213 animals (22 cattle, 14 buffaloes, 105 goats and 72 pigs). The livestock sheds were cleaned using a high-pressure jet washer to maintain hygienic housing conditions. The wastewater generated during shed cleaning was collected and reused for irrigation of fodder plots, promoting water conservation and resource recycling. Livestock urine was collected and utilized for fodder irrigation to facilitate nutrient recycling. Animal dung from all livestock units was collected and transported to the vermicompost unit for conversion into organic manure. These activities promote efficient utilization of biological wastes, reduce indiscriminate waste disposal, conserve water and nutrients, and support sustainable livestock farming and fodder production. Thus, the initiative represents an integrated, environment-friendly approach to livestock waste management and a circular bio-resource utilization system.

ICAR-IIFSR, Modipuram, Meerut

The cleanliness drive involved collecting, organizing, and loading dry garden waste into a cart for disposal. The collected waste included dry leaves and large palm fronds, helping to maintain cleanliness in the park and the surrounding areas of the Institute.

 

 

ICAR-Research Complex for NEH Region, Umiam, Meghalaya

 As theme of this year’s campaign was disposing of electronic waste, efforts were made to collect, segregate and dispose these items to authorised recyclers, refurbishers and developers for earning maximum revenue.

ICAR-National Meat Research Institute, Hyderabad

  

For wider dissemination and outreach, ICAR Headquarters has issued Press releases on activities undertaken under the campaign, while ICAR institutes and establishments have publicized their activities through local print media, banners and other communication channels. At both Headquarters and institutional levels, the campaign and its activities are also being disseminated through social media platforms, including Facebook, X and Instagram, thereby extending the message of Swachhata beyond the ICAR network to wider and more diverse audiences, particularly digitally engaged audiences and the younger generation.

2325820.title: CCO's SUVIKALP Initiative Advances Sustainable Mine Repurposing, Receives SKOCH Gold Award 2026
2325820.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
CCO's SUVIKALP Initiative Advances Sustainable Mine Repurposing, Receives SKOCH Gold Award 2026
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 12:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Coal Controller Organisation (CCO), under the Ministry of Coal, has undertaken initiatives to promote scientific mine closure and sustainable repurposing of post-mining land.

CCO has developed SUVIKALP, an in-house Mine Repurposing Tool, to assist stakeholders in selecting suitable mine repurposing projects through a structured and data-driven decision-making process. The tool evaluates and ranks repurposing projects based on multiple technical, environmental, social and economic criteria.

Once a suitable project is identified, users can explore implementation pathways through PRISM (Post-Mining Repurposing Implementation Strategy Model). PRISM provides project concepts, implementation approaches, case studies, sample Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), tender documents and information on agencies working in similar sectors.

The innovation and utility of SUVIKALP received national recognition through the SKOCH Gold Award 2026 under the category “Digital Operational Efficiency – Data Driven Decision Making” on 26 September 2026. The SKOCH Awards recognise excellence in governance, technology, innovation and transformational initiatives delivering public value.

CCO has also undertaken the SUVIKALP Samvaad Webinar Series as a structured knowledge-sharing and capacity-building initiative to support informed decision-making on mine closure and sustainable repurposing. The national webinar series brought together coal companies, government officials, technical experts, academic institutions and other stakeholders to share practical solutions, innovative models and best practices related to post-mining land use.

A total of 12 thematic webinars were conducted under the series, covering the RECLAIM and L.I.V.E.S. frameworks, SUVIKALP Mine Repurposing Tool, PMU establishment, community engagement, tourism and destination development, livelihood opportunities, financing mechanisms, innovative uses of abandoned mine voids, and national and international experiences of mine transition.

The series has strengthened the institutional understanding of coal companies on the multidimensional aspects of mine closure, moving beyond regulatory compliance towards environmental restoration, livelihood generation, community development and economic diversification. Expert-led deliberations and knowledge exchange have provided practical insights and scalable approaches for planning and implementing sustainable repurposing projects.

The initiatives support the Ministry of Coal's vision of transforming closed coal mines into productive assets and enabling sustainable regional development.

2325711.title: SARAS Mela 2026
2325711.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
SARAS Mela 2026
Taking Rural Women’s Enterprises to the National Markets
Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 11:11AM by PIB Delhi

The SARAS Melas organized under the Centre's DAY-NRLM connect rural women entrepreneurs with wider markets, buyers, and business opportunities. The Vijayawada edition marks the first National SARAS Mela outside Delhi-NCR, bringing together women entrepreneurs from 34 states and UTs. The platform strengthens DAY-NRLM’s efforts to promote sustainable livelihoods and supports the Lakhpati Didi vision of income growth. Dedicated pavilions offer opportunities for business learning, institutional support, and enterprise development. Digital platforms like eSARAS extend market access beyond physical events, helping rural women take their products to wider markets.

 

Where Rural Enterprise Meets Opportunity

India’s rural economy is rich in traditional skills, crafts and entrepreneurial talent. Women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs) help bring this talent into local economies. Their products range from handlooms and handicrafts to processed foods and other locally made goods. Yet making a product is only the first step. Rural entrepreneurs also need customers, market information, and opportunities to grow. SARAS Melas help bridge this gap by bringing women-led enterprises closer to consumers, buyers, and institutions. Organised by the government under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), SARAS Melas have evolved over nearly three decades. They are no longer only exhibitions. They offer a space to sell products, understand consumer preferences, build business connections, and explore wider markets.

The National SARAS Mela in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, marks a new step in this journey as it is the first National SARAS Mela to be organised outside the Delhi-NCR region. The event is running from 13 October 2026 to 31 October 2026 at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada. Around 1,500 women SHG entrepreneurs and Lakhpati Didis from 34 States and UTs are showcasing their products through more than 650 stalls. The Mela features regional textiles, handicrafts, natural and processed foods, and other rural products. An India Food Court, cultural showcases, and dedicated learning spaces add to the experience.

The decentralisation of the National SARAS Mela reflects a wider development approach: taking national platforms closer to producers and consumers across India. It connects local skills with new markets while supporting the growth of women-led enterprises. This event paves the way for further decentralisation of other national events and is in line with the approach of conducting international events like BRICS and G20 meetings at regional levels.

 

From Rural Livelihoods to Market Access: The Role of DAY-NRLM

DAY-NRLM is the government’s flagship programme for reducing rural poverty and promoting women’s economic empowerment. It works through SHGs and their federations, while supporting financial inclusion and sustainable livelihoods. The Mission helps women access skills, finance, technology and livelihood opportunities. It also strengthens the market ecosystem around women-led enterprises through product visibility, branding and links with physical, digital and institutional markets.

This market connection matters because enterprise growth depends on more than production. Women need opportunities to sell beyond their immediate communities. They also benefit from feedback, better product presentation, and connections with buyers. SARAS Melas provide a practical bridge between these needs and market opportunities. They bring SHG enterprises, consumers, institutional buyers and other stakeholders together. Entrepreneurs can sell directly, study customer preferences and explore partnerships that may continue after the event.

 

From 65 Beneficiaries to a National Marketplace

The SARAS journey began in 1999, when the first National SARAS Mela was organised in Delhi with around 65 beneficiaries. Since then, the platform has expanded to national, regional, state and district levels. As on date, a total of 117 National SARAS Melas and annual sales exceeding ₹200 crore have been recorded. States and Union Territories also organise a minimum of two State-level SARAS Melas a year, bringing the national average to around 50 events annually. Regional and district-level events bring selling opportunities closer to local producers. Together, these formats support market discovery, branding, buyer–seller linkages and enterprise development.

 

Lakhpati Didi: Making Livelihoods More Sustainable

The Lakhpati Didi initiative is an outcome-oriented livelihood initiative under DAY-NRLM. It builds on the network of women organised through SHGs and their federations. Its focus is to help women and their households achieve sustainable income through diversified livelihood opportunities. A Lakhpati Didi is an SHG member whose household earns at least ₹1 lakh annually on a sustainable basis. The assessment covers at least four agricultural seasons and/or business cycles. The initiative received national impetus in August 2023, when the government announced an ambition to create two crore Lakhpati Didis. The target was raised to three crore in the Interim Budget 2024-25. Subsequently, the initiative achieved the three-crore milestone by December 2025.

In February 2026, the government announced an enhanced target of six crore Lakhpati Didis. This next phase places greater importance on sustaining income gains and helping enterprises grow. Market access, product visibility, branding, and reliable sales channels are important to this effort. SARAS Melas support this transition from livelihood creation to enterprise growth. They can also create opportunities for bulk orders, institutional sales, and longer-term market connections. The Vijayawada Mela brings this connection to life through dedicated spaces for successful entrepreneurs, business learning, and institutional support. Women can share their experience, learn new practices, and explore ways to strengthen their enterprises.

 

Vijayawada: A National Marketplace with a Regional Reach

The Vijayawada Mela brings products and traditions from across India into one marketplace. Visitors can explore Phulkari from Punjab, Pashmina from Jammu and Kashmir, Ikat and Telia textiles from Telangana, and Paunchei from Mizoram. The stalls also feature Meenakari, Dokra, brasswork, woodcraft and traditional paintings.

A 16-foot installation titled “SHAKTI - The Spirit of Lakhpati Didi” forms a signature feature of this Mela. It symbolises the collective strength of women who preserve traditional craftsmanship and turn their skills into livelihoods, independence and prosperity.

The Mela is supported by government partners, including the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) and the National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (NIRDPR). Its design combines direct sales with learning, demonstrations, and connections to institutions. The aim is to make the event useful not only for visitors, but also for the entrepreneurs seeking to build sustainable businesses.

 

Spaces That Connect Products, Skills and Opportunity

The Vijayawada National SARAS Mela is going beyond a conventional exhibition and retail format by creating a series of dedicated thematic, knowledge and engagement spaces. These spaces are providing opportunities for enterprise showcasing, peer learning, knowledge exchange, convergence with government and market stakeholders, live demonstrations, and structured buyer–seller interactions.

Lakhpati Didi Pavilion: Learning from Enterprise Journeys

The Lakhpati Didi Pavilion showcases women who have built successful enterprises. It features entrepreneurs earning more than ₹10 lakh annually, including women earning over ₹1 crore. These women share their journeys, products, business models, and market strategies with other SHG members. Their stories highlight different routes to enterprise growth, including agriculture, non-farm livelihoods, food processing, handicrafts, handlooms and services. Peer learning can help women identify approaches suited to their own skills and circumstances.

Learning and Knowledge Pavilion: Building Business Skills

Strong products need strong business practices. The Learning and Knowledge Pavilion is designed for workshops, expert talks, masterclasses and experience-sharing sessions among SHG entrepreneurs, State Rural Livelihood Missions (SRLMs), buyers and other stakeholders. Topics include packaging, branding, preparing business proposals, e-commerce and social media marketing. Further, engagement with public institutions and private-sector organisations is also encouraged. These include NABARD, FICCI, CII, ITC, Hindustan Unilever, Amazon and Flipkart. Such interactions can expose entrepreneurs to practical tools for improving product presentation and reaching customers.

Convergence Pavilion: Connecting Women with Support

Growing an enterprise often requires more than market access. Entrepreneurs also need credit, skills, technology, quality certification, and government support. The Convergence Pavilion brings SHG entrepreneurs together with relevant departments, financial institutions, development agencies and technical institutions. These organisations and platforms include the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Ministry of Textiles, ONDC, Government eMarketplace (GeM) and TRIFED. The pavilion is intended to help women understand relevant schemes, services and support systems.

Demonstration Pavilion: Showing How Products Are Made

A finished product often carries a story of skill, time and technique. The Demonstration Pavilion lets visitors see that process directly. Women entrepreneurs and artisans are demonstrating live traditional and contemporary production methods. These activities include pottery, needlework, and mirror-work embroidery. Live demonstrations by the Lakhpati Didis create opportunities for practical learning and knowledge exchange. They also help visitors appreciate the craftsmanship behind handmade products, and the “Demo and Live Learning Area” offers a special experience.

 

India Food Court: Regional Flavours and Women’s Enterprise

Food is another route through which rural enterprise reaches consumers. The India Food Court features 50 food stalls showcasing regional cuisines being prepared in traditional ways using pure spices. The event brings together more than 200 first-generation women food-service entrepreneurs from over 28 states and UTs. Visitors can explore street favourites such as Gol Gappe, Chaat and Kebabs. Regional dishes include Litti Chokha from Bihar, Hyderabadi Dum Biryani, Mushroom Pitha from Assam, and Makke Di Roti with Saag from Punjab. Other examples include Vana Sundari from Attappadi in Kerala and Chausela from Chhattisgarh. The food court gives women an opportunity to present regional culinary traditions in a national setting. It also brings the business of food preparation and service into the wider story of women-led entrepreneurship.

 

Cultural Showcases: Celebrating India’s Diversity

Cultural programmes feature traditional art forms, crafts, textiles, music and dance from participating regions, creating an immersive national experience for visitors. These showcases celebrate the heritage behind many of the products on display. They also facilitate participating states in presenting their distinct cultural identities.

 

Digital Integration: From Physical Stalls to Digital Markets

Digital payments are an important catalyst for business activities at the SARAS Mela. UPI transactions support convenient and transparent payments, and the food court primarily operates through cashless transactions. At the same time, keeping in view the convenience of elderly citizens and visitors who may prefer cash payments, coupon-based cash payment facilities are also available, ensuring an inclusive and seamless experience for all.

Further, A market opportunity should not end when a Mela closes. Digital channels can help enterprises reach customers beyond the event and across geographical boundaries. The SARAS ecosystem, therefore, combines physical Melas with the SARAS Gallery and e-commerce channels. The eSARAS platform provides an online route for customers to discover and purchase products made by SHG entrepreneurs. This extends the market-access approach beyond face-to-face sales and can help products remain visible after the Mela.

A dedicated SARAS Mela Digital App was introduced in 2025. It supports SHG nominations, attendance management, and the sharing of event-related information.  Together, physical events and digital channels offer complementary routes to market. The SARAS Mela creates direct contact with customers and buyers. Online channels can help extend product discovery and sales beyond the event.

 

Taking National Market Access to the Regions

The Vijayawada National SARAS Mela represents an expansion of the market-access platform into a new region. Organising national events in different locations can bring them closer to local consumers, buyers and institutional partners. It can also help producers from different States gain exposure to wider markets. This approach supports the broader objectives of DAY-NRLM and the Lakhpati Didi initiative. Women need sustainable livelihoods, but they also need ways to improve product value and expand sales. Platforms that combine selling, learning, and institutional connections can contribute to that process.

This National SARAS Mela (outside the Delhi NCR region) is a landmark initiative taken by the Government during the SEVA Pakhwada beginning from 2nd October 2026. SARAS Melas also promote the vision of Vocal for Local and Atmanirbhar Bharat. They give consumers a direct way to discover rural products and meet the women entrepreneurs behind them. They create opportunities to preserve traditional skills while strengthening women-led enterprises. At its heart, the National SARAS Mela is about the women behind every product, craft, and enterprise, and the journey from skill to enterprise, enterprise to market, and market to sustainable livelihood.

Posted On: 21 OCT 2026 7:50AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam today, drawing a  parallel between coconut trees and noble people to highlight the virtues of lifelong gratitude and selfless service.

The Prime Minister wrote on X;

"प्रथमवयसि पीतं तोयमल्पं स्मरन्तः शिरसि निहितभारा नारिकेला नराणाम्।

ददति जलमनल्पास्वादमाजीवितान्तं न हि कृतमुपकारं साधवो विस्मरन्ति॥"  

Just as a coconut tree remembers, throughout its life, the small amount of water it received in its early stage and even while bearing a heavy burden upon its head continues to offer sweet water to humankind, in the same way truly noble individuals, especially in reverence to the great souls who made sacrifices, never forget the benefaction done to them. Holding deep gratitude for their sacrifice, austerity and dedication, they align their lives with their ideals and remain ever grateful for that benevolence through their actions and spirit of devoted service.

2325589.title: PM Modi-led Govt is striving to make India a nation that combines prosperity, knowledge and strength with a commitment to global peace & well-being of humanity: Raksha Mantri
2325589.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
PM Modi-led Govt is striving to make India a nation that combines prosperity, knowledge and strength with a commitment to global peace & well-being of humanity: Raksha Mantri
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 8:53PM by PIB Delhi

“Guided by the philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, India aspires to become a nation that combines prosperity, knowledge & strength with a commitment to global peace and the well-being of humanity,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh while addressing the Indian diaspora in Dushanbe, Tajikistan on October 20, 2026. He emphasised that India’s economic transformation, reform-driven governance, technological advancement and growing global stature under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership are paving the way towards the realisation of this vision.

Highlighting India’s growth trajectory, Raksha Mantri stated that the country contributes more than 16 per cent to global economic growth and is growing at approximately 7.8 per cent, even as several major economies face a slowdown. Referring to the changing global trade landscape, the Raksha Mantri said that India has entered into Free Trade Agreements with 38 countries, opening new markets for Indian manufacturers and producers. He stated that the India-UK and India-EU trade agreements, which are expected to eliminate tariffs on 99 per cent of Indian exports to these markets, would strengthen the country’s trade prospects and global economic partnerships.

On the transformation in governance and policymaking over the last decade, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that India has moved from an era of ‘policy paralysis’ to a ‘reform express’ driven by a clear policy direction. “For us, reforms are not a compulsion; they are a conviction,” he said.

Raksha Mantri noted that the current account deficit, which exceeded four per cent of GDP 12-13 years ago, declined to 0.61 per cent in the previous financial year. India’s foreign exchange reserves have crossed US$700 billion, while the banking system is in its strongest-ever position, he added.

Highlighting India’s progress in defence manufacturing, Shri Rajnath Singh said that defence exports have reached a record Rs 38,424 crore, with defence production surging to Rs 1.80 lakh crore. He underlined that the number of start-ups has grown from a few hundred before 2014 to more than 2.5 lakh, and nearly half of these start-ups originate from smaller cities and towns, while more than 45 per cent have at least one woman director or partner. He said that affordable mobile data and wider connectivity have enabled more Indians to access opportunities, encouraging innovation, nurturing new talent and generating fresh solutions.

Raksha Mantri also highlighted the impact of inclusive development, stating that approximately 25 crore people have been lifted out of poverty over the past decade. He underscored the role of the JAM Trinity and Direct Benefit Transfer in delivering government assistance directly into beneficiaries’ bank accounts, reducing corruption and enhancing transparency and convenience.

Shri Rajnath Singh noted that India’s renewable energy capacity has increased from approximately 75 GW in 2014 to nearly 300 GW. He stated that India is advancing rapidly towards semiconductor manufacturing through the Semicon India programme and the India Semiconductor Mission. “We’re moving towards manufacturing both ships and chips, strengthening our position in strategic sectors,” he said.

On India’s digital transformation, Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that the country has emerged as a global hub for real-time digital transactions. He stated that the value of UPI transactions has risen from Rs 7,000 crore in 2016-17 to Rs Rs 314 lakh crore in 2025-26, reflecting the scale of India’s transition towards a seamless, less-paper and less-cash economy. He also underlined the unprecedented expansion of India’s infrastructure, including railways, roads, airports, ports and broadband connectivity.

Underscoring India’s achievements in science and space technology, Shri Rajnath Singh referred to the successes of Chandrayaan and Aditya-L1. He exuded confidence in the progress of preparations for the Gaganyaan human spaceflight mission.

Raksha Mantri described India as a confident nation with which countries across the world seek to build strong and positive relations. He said that people of Indian origin serve as cultural ambassadors, carrying India’s values and traditions across the globe while contributing to the development of their host countries.

Shri Rajnath Singh appreciated the efforts being made towards forging closer cultural and people-to-people ties and noted that India and Tajikistan remain connected through a strong bond of friendship cemented by popularity of Indian songs, music, literature and cinema among Tajik people. He underlined that India and Tajikistan share longstanding cordial relations in which the contribution of the Indian diaspora remains a strong element that connects the two countries.

On the occasion, Raksha Mantri also felicitated Prof Habibullo Rajabov, a renowned Indologist and first Padma Shri awardee from Tajikistan, underlining his valuable contribution in the field of Hindi literature and education including an in-depth study of philology. The event included cultural performances by Indian and Tajik artists.

2325573.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participates in Vijaya Dashami celebrations in Delhi
2325573.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participates in Vijaya Dashami celebrations in Delhi
Vijaya Dashami celebrates the victory of good over evil; It reminds us of the enduring strength of truth and righteousness: PM
For us, this is not merely a festival; this is the life energy of India: PM
Lord Ram has given us such ideals which are incomparable in the history of humanity: PM
We have to keep the service of the poor and the deprived paramount: PM
When we stand with truth and humanity, then in the end, victory is ours: PM
The vision of ‘Ram Se Rashtra’ and ‘Dev Se Desh’ that we have conceived, we will definitely fulfill it: PM
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in Vijaya Dashami celebrations in Delhi. Addressing the Vijayadashami celebrations at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, the Prime Minister commenced his address by extending his warmest festive wishes to the entire nation on the auspicious occasion. "I extend my heartfelt greetings of Vijayadashami to all the countrymen,” remarked Shri Modi.

Describing how every village and city across India is immersed in the staging of Ramlilas, the Prime Minister highlighted the tradition of keeping Lord Ram’s ideals alive, proclaiming the end of tyranny and terror, and upholding the victory of eternal truth over falsehood. He invited the gathering to join him in chanting praises to the deity as citizens nationwide celebrate the triumph of righteousness over unrighteousness. "For us, this is not merely a festival; this is the life energy of India,” asserted PM Modi.

Reflecting on the millennia-old devotion of India’s culture and ancestors toward Lord Shri Ram, the Prime Minister noted that this deep reverence extends far beyond his victory over the demon king Ravana. He emphasized that the enduring faith of the nation is anchored in the timeless values Lord Ram imparted to the world. "Lord Ram has given us such ideals which are incomparable in the history of humanity,” observed Shri Modi.

Recalling the immense hardships Lord Shri Ram faced without ever forsaking truth and morality, the Prime Minister quoted the Sanskrit verse to illustrate his equanimity during both his royal coronation and his forest exile. He highlighted how Lord Ram upheld righteousness through every crisis, embraced Nishadraj, and honored Mother Shabari during his time in the forest. "He established benchmarks of mercy, compassion, love, and harmony,” remarked PM Modi.

Detailing the establishment of Ramrajya upon Lord Ram's return as the King of Ayodhya, the Prime Minister described it as the ultimate benchmark of non-discriminatory governance where everyone receives justice and equal opportunity, and where power serves public welfare rather than authority, as immortalized in Goswami Tulsidas’s verse “Daihik Daivik Bhautik Tapa, Ram Raj Nahin Kahuhi Byapa.” He urged the administration to follow these ideals of Maryada Purushottam by treating the public as divine under the mantra of Nagrik Devo Bhava. "We have to keep the service of the poor and the deprived paramount,” asserted Shri Modi.

Drawing profound lessons of self-reliance from Lord Ram’s journey across the ocean to Lanka, the Prime Minister explained that instead of relying on others during a crisis, Lord Ram awakened collective public participation (Janbhagidari) and pooled available resources to achieve the impossible through faith, capability, and unwavering resolve. He called upon citizens to adopt this fundamental mantra of hard work and resourcefulness to fulfill public aspirations and achieve the goals of a Viksit Bharat and an Aatmanirbhar Bharat. "Lord Ram taught us that the difficulties on the path cannot stop our journey,” affirmed PM Modi.

Linking national progress to a strong sense of self-respect rooted in cultural heritage, the Prime Minister detailed the government's active campaign to preserve India's identity by repatriating over 650 ancient idols over the past 12 years. He also celebrated the growing global recognition of India's cultural centers, noting the inclusion of numerous domestic sites on the UNESCO World Heritage list and the inscription of Deepavali on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list last year through the collective willpower of crores of Indians. "We have to continue working with this same dedication in the future,” noted Shri Modi.

Invoking the courageous spirit of Vijayadashami that guarantees triumph when standing with truth and humanity, the Prime Minister quoted the Vedic mantra “Samano Mantrah Samitih Samani” to urge all national institutions and political parties to unite in the national interest. He called upon citizens to adopt a 'Nation First' pledge to jointly identify and defeat the enemies of Maa Bharati, specifically forces that harm national honor, divide society, and harbor hatred toward Indian culture. "When we stand with truth and humanity, then in the end, victory is ours,” asserted PM Modi.

Concluding his address with deep conviction, the Prime Minister recalled the sacred resolutions taken during the Pran Pratishtha ceremony at the Ayodhya temple and extended his final Dussehra greetings alongside chants of Jai Siya Ram and Bharat Mata Ki Jai. He expressed absolute confidence in realizing the nation's spiritual and developmental vision. "The vision of ‘Ram Se Rashtra’ and ‘Dev Se Desh’ that we have conceived, we will definitely fulfill it,” affirmed Shri Modi.

2325534.title: 8 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 To Begin in Guwahati Tomorrow
2325534.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
8 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 To Begin in Guwahati Tomorrow
75 Artisans, Including 31 Women, to Showcase Around 40 Varieties of Handloom and Handicraft Products
Mela to Promote Market Access, Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Livelihoods for Artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs)
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 7:55PM by PIB Delhi

The 08 days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will begin in State Capital Guwahati of Assam, from tomorrow. The Mela is being organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, until October 28 Wednesday.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela will be open to public at Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati, from 11 A.M. onwards till 9 O’ Clock. He said the visitors will explore the diverse range of traditional products to purchase the creations and support the artisans.

He said the Mela will bring together artisans from across the country, including the North-Eastern States, to showcase India’s rich and diverse heritage of traditional handicrafts and handloom products.

The Official said a total of 75 artisans, including 31 women artisans, are participating in the Mela, displaying approximately 40 varieties of handloom and handicraft products.

He said the event will provide participating artisans with a platform to exhibit and sell their products directly to visitors, establish connections with prospective customers and explore opportunities to expand their market reach. By facilitating direct interaction between artisans and consumers, the Mela seeks to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and improve livelihood opportunities for participating artisans, he added.

The Official said the Guwahati edition will feature a wide range of traditional crafts and handloom products representing different regions of India. The participation of artisans from the North-Eastern States, alongside those from other parts of the country, will provide visitors with an opportunity to appreciate the diversity of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and cultural heritage, he added.

He said the event aims to also encourage greater appreciation of the skills and creativity of artisans whose work contributes to preserving traditional knowledge and craft practices.

The Official further said a key focus of the Mela will be the promotion of BHARAT-TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme), an initiative aimed at facilitating the marketing of products made by artisans belonging to the target groups through physical outlets and e-commerce platforms. By promoting access to wider markets and digital channels, the initiative seeks to strengthen market linkages, expand customer outreach and create additional opportunities for artisans to enhance their earnings. It also supports the preservation and promotion of traditional arts and crafts by connecting artisans and their products with evolving consumer markets, he said.

Shilp Samagam Mela (SSM-2026) is an important initiative of the Ministry to provide marketing support to artisans and beneficiaries associated with its three National Corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), and the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC).

The first edition of SSM 2026 concluded in Mysuru on October 19, with thousands of visitors thronging the nine days Mela at Dasara Exhibition Ground, Mysuru in Karnataka.

Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s principle of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas”, the Mela seeks to promote the economic empowerment of artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs). It provides a dedicated platform for these communities to showcase their skills, market their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance through sustainable livelihood opportunities.

In addition to promoting the sale of traditional products, the Mela will help create awareness among visitors and participating communities about the welfare, financial assistance and development schemes implemented by the Ministry and its three National Corporations. The initiative seeks to complement financial and developmental support with market-oriented interventions, enabling artisans to translate their traditional skills and craftsmanship into viable livelihood opportunities, the official said.

It is pertinent to mention that through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to advance its efforts towards the socio-economic empowerment of disadvantaged  communities by promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating market access and supporting sustainable livelihoods.

The Mela is expected to enhance the visibility of participating artisans, expand awareness of their products and encourage greater public engagement with India’s rich handloom and handicraft traditions.

विजयदशमी के इस पावन पर्व पर मैं प्रभु श्रीराम, माँ जानकी और बजरंग बली के चरणों में प्रणाम करता हूँ। इस पवित्र वातावरण में, मैं सभी देशवासियों को विजयदशमी की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ देता हूँ।

साथियों,

आज भारत का कोना-कोना राममय है। गाँव-गाँव, शहर-शहर रामलीला के रस में देश डूबा हुआ है। देशभर में रामलीलाओं का मंचन, प्रभु श्रीराम के आदर्शों को जीवंत रखने की परंपरा, अत्याचार और आतंक के अंत का उद्घोष और असत्य पर सत्य सनातन की विजय का विश्वास, हमारे लिए ये केवल त्योहार नहीं है, ये भारत की प्राण ऊर्जा है। इसलिए, आज जब देश का जन-जन अधर्म पर धर्म की विजय का उद्घोष कर रहा है, तो आइये, फिर एक बार मेरे साथ बोलिए -

सियावर रामचंद्र की जय!

सियावर रामचंद्र की जय!

सियावर रामचंद्र की जय!

साथियों,

इस देश ने, इसकी संस्कृति ने और इसके पूर्वजों ने हजारों वर्षों से प्रभु श्रीराम की उपासना की है। ये आस्था केवल इसलिए नहीं है कि, श्रीराम ने राक्षसराज रावण का अंत किया था। ये आस्था इसलिए भी है, क्योंकि प्रभु राम ने हमें ऐसे आदर्श दिये, जो मानवता के इतिहास में अतुलनीय है।

साथियों,

प्रभु श्रीराम ने अपने जीवन में कितनी ही कठिनाइयों का सामना किया, लेकिन उन्होंने सच्चाई और नीति का रास्ता कभी नहीं छोड़ा। उनका चरित्र ही ऐसा है, ‘प्रसन्नतां या न गत अभिषेकतः तथा,न मम्ले वनवास दुःखतः॥’ अर्थात्, प्रभु राम के चेहरे पर न राजपद पाने की प्रसन्नता हुई, और न वन जाने से उन्हें कोई दुख हुआ। उन्होंने हर संकट को सहकर भी धर्म का पालन किया और सत्य की स्थापना की। जब हमारे राम जंगल गए, तो वहाँ उन्होंने निषादराज को गले लगाया, माता शबरी को सम्मान दिया। उन्होंने दया, करुणा, प्रेम और सौहार्द के मानदंड स्थापित किए। और जब वापस आकर प्रभु राम अयोध्या के राजा बने, तो ऐसे रामराज्य की स्थापना की, जो आज भी सुशासन का, गवर्नेंस का मानदंड माना जाता है। रामराज्य अर्थात् ऐसा शासन, जहां किसी के प्रति भेदभाव नहीं हो, जहां सबको न्याय मिले, जहां सबको समान अवसर मिलें, जहाँ सत्ता का उद्देश्य शासन करना नहीं, जन-कल्याण का हो। और इसलिए ही गोस्वामी तुलसीदास जी ने कहा था - ‘दैहिक दैविक भौतिक तापा। राम राज नहिं काहुहि ब्यापा॥’ यही मर्यादा पुरुषोत्तम प्रभु श्रीराम का आदर्श है। इसलिए हमें हमेशा जनता को जनार्दन मानकर, नागरिक देवो भव के मंत्र पर आगे बढ़ना है। हमें गरीब, वंचित की सेवा को सर्वोपरि रखना है।

साथियों,

प्रभु राम के जीवन से हमें बहुत बड़ी सीख मिलती है। संकट कितना भी बड़ा क्यों ना हो, चुनौती कितनी भी कठिन क्यों ना हो, हमें दूसरों के भरोसे नहीं बैठना है, हमें अपना सामर्थ्य पहचानना है, हमें अपने संसाधनों पर विश्वास करना है, अपने संकल्प को शक्ति बनाना है, और अपने परिश्रम से समाधान निकालना है। प्रभु राम ने हमें सिखाया कि रास्ते की कठिनाइयाँ, हमारी यात्रा को रोक नहीं सकतीं। समुद्र सामने था, लंका दूर थी, लेकिन संकल्प अडिग था। इसलिए राम जी ने जनता की सामूहिक शक्ति को जगाया, जनभागीदारी को अपना संबल बनाया, उपलब्ध संसाधनों को जोड़ा। और असंभव लगने वाले लक्ष्य को संभव बनाया। यही सफलता का मूल मंत्र है। अपनी शक्ति पर विश्वास, अपने सामर्थ्य पर भरोसा, अपने संसाधनों का सही उपयोग और अपने लक्ष्य के प्रति अटूट संकल्प। आज हमें भी इसी मंत्र को लेकर आगे बढ़ना है। हमारे सामने विकसित भारत का लक्ष्य है, हमारे सामने आत्मनिर्भर भारत का लक्ष्य है। हमें जनशक्ति से जनकल्याण करते हुए, जनता की हर आकांक्षाओं को पूरा करना है और इसके लिए भी हमें भगवान राम से ही प्रेरणा भी लेनी है।

साथियों,

एक राष्ट्र तभी प्रगति करता है, जब उसके पास आत्मसम्मान का भाव होता है। और इस आत्मसम्मान में बहुत बड़ी भूमिका उसकी विरासत की होती है। इसलिए, आज देश अपनी विरासत और पहचान को भी संरक्षित करने में जुटा है। सदियों तक हमारी धरोहरों को लूटकर विदेश ले जाया गया, लेकिन आज हम अपनी उन धरोहरों को वापिस ला रहे हैं। बीते 12 वर्षों में साढ़े छह सौ से ज्यादा प्राचीन मूर्तियों को भारत वापिस लाया गया है। इसी तरह, भारत अपने सांस्कृतिक केन्द्रों को दुनिया में नई पहचान दिलवा रहा है। बीते वर्षों में, हमारे कितने ही स्थानों को यूनेस्को वर्ल्ड हेरिटेज साइट्स की लिस्ट में शामिल किया गया है। पिछले साल दीपावली को भी यूनेस्को ने मानवता की अमूर्त सांस्कृतिक विरासत की सूची में शामिल किया है। ये करोड़ों भारतीयों की सामूहिक इच्छाशक्ति का ही परिणाम है। हमें इसी निष्ठा से आगे भी काम करना है।

साथियों,

विजयदशमी, विजय का पर्व है, जीत का पर्व है। ये पर्व हमें साहस देता है कि शत्रु कितना भी बड़ा क्यों न हो, लेकिन जब हम सच्चाई और मानवता के साथ होते हैं, तो अंत में जीत हमारी होती है। विजयदशमी की यही भावना हमेशा से भारत की विचारधारा रही है। हमारे ऋषियों ने हमें प्रेरणा दी है - ‘समानो मन्त्रः समितिः समानी समानं मनः सह चित्तमेषाम्।’ अर्थात्, हमारे विचार समान हों, हमारी समितियां,अर्थात् राष्ट्र की सभी संस्थाएं, सभी राजनीतिक दल, राष्ट्रहित के लिए एक साथ खड़े हों। हमें इसी भावना पर चलना होगा, हमें देश के दुश्मनों के साथ मिलकर लड़ना होगा। देश के मान-सम्मान को चोट पहुंचाने वाली ताक़तें, समाज को बांटने वाले लोग, हमारी संस्कृति से नफरत करने वाले की मानसिकता, ये देश के दुश्मन हैं। आज विजयदशमी के शुभ पर्व पर हमें अपना संकल्प फिर दोहराना है, हमें मॉं भारती के शत्रुओं को पहचानना होगा, उन्हें परास्त करना होगा। और राष्ट्र प्रथम का संकल्प लेते हुए, सबको एक साथ आना होगा। मुझे विश्वास है, अयोध्या मंदिर में प्राण प्रतिष्ठा समारोह के दौरान ‘राम से राष्ट्र’ और ‘देव से देश’ की जो संकल्पना हमने की है, उसे हम जरूर पूरा करेंगे। मैं एक बार फिर सभी देशवासियों को दशहरे की बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूँ।

जय सिया राम !

जय सिया राम !

जय सिया राम !

भारत माता की जय।

भारत माता की जय।

बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

2325520.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah participates in Vijayadashami festival in Ludhiana, Punjab, and performs burning of the symbolic Ravana of ‘Chitta’
2325520.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah participates in Vijayadashami festival in Ludhiana, Punjab, and performs burning of the symbolic Ravana of ‘Chitta’
I have been hearing since childhood that if one wants to see Ravana Dahan, one should go to Ludhiana, where the Ramlila Committee has been organising the programme for 200 years

Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 7:47PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today participated in the Vijayadashami festival in Ludhiana, Punjab, and performed the burning of the symbolic Ravana of ‘Chitta’ (Drugs).

In his address, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that in our tradition, the burning of Ravana’s effigy is a symbol of the victory of good over evil. Vijayadashami is the day for every person to eliminate the ego, pride, greed and other evils within themselves. On this very day, thousands of years ago, Lord Shri Ram achieved victory over Ravana, and since then the entire world has been celebrating Lord Shri Ram’s victory as the triumph of good over evil. He said that he has heard since childhood that if you want to see Ravana Dahan, go to Ludhiana, where the Ramlila Committee has been organising the Ravana Dahan programme for 200 years.

Shri Amit Shah said that today he met families at three places in Punjab who had lost their sons in the fight against drugs. He said that the tears in the eyes of those relatives, their questions, and their pain are enough to shake anyone to the core. Shri Shah said that the Punjab government has handed over the investigation of one murder to the CBI. He urged the Punjab government to hand over the investigation of the remaining two murders to the CBI as well. The Home Minister expressed confidence that justice will be done in these cases. Once the investigation is handed over to the CBI, no matter how big a person is involved in these murders, the Modi government will track them down and put them behind bars.

Union Home Minister said that on this Vijayadashami itself, we take this resolve that by 31 December 2029 we will free the entire Punjab from the drug trade and make it a drug-free Punjab. He said that there can be no greater tribute than this to these three brave individuals who lost their lives. Shri Shah said that if the people of Punjab provide information about the drug trade on the Narcotics Control Bureau’s toll-free helpline, the Modi government will take action on it.

Shri Amit Shah said that the Modi government has a record of fulfilling what it has promised. Article 370 and 35A are gone, terrorism is on the verge of being eliminated, and we have ended Naxalism. He said that now we will also eliminate the drug trade.

2325463.title: 9 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Concludes In Mysuru Karnataka
2325463.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
9 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Concludes In Mysuru Karnataka
Thousands Visit Mela Showcasing Traditional Handicrafts, Handloom Products of Artisans from 12 States/UTs
Mela Featured 83 Stalls, Including 80 Stalls Allotted To Artisans, Among Them 37 Women Artisans
Hon’ble Minister Ramdas Athawale, Union Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Visits Shilp Samagam Mela Mysuru
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Nine Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 successfully concluded with thousands of people visiting Dasara Exhibition Grounds at Mysuru in Karnataka. The Mela was organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.

The Mela aimed to provide a marketing platform for traditional handicraft and handloom products made by beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis, including artisans supported by the three National Corporations functioning under the Ministry, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

Deputy General Manager in the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) Shri Rajnish Banker said the initiative sought to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for the target groups.

He said the Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022, and 975 artisans have been benefited through 13 such fairs organised so far.

Shri Banker said the Mysuru edition was the first Shilp Samagam Mela of the financial year 2026–27.

The Official said a total of 83 stalls had been put up at the Mela, out of which 80 were allotted to artisans, including 37 women artisans. Food stalls serving traditional delicacies had also been set up for visitors.

The Mela featured artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, he added.

The DGM informed that the exhibition showcased a wide range of traditional products, including handicraft items, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed products, Kanjivaram sarees, leather goods, wooden toys, bags and purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers.

The platform enables artisans to display their products to a wider audience and connect with prospective customers, while promoting India's diverse cultural heritage and traditional skills.

The official further said that Shilp Samagam Mela also serves as a platform to disseminate information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and its three national corporations—NSFDC, NBCFDC and NSKFDC. The initiative seeks to enhance awareness about available assistance and development opportunities for eligible beneficiaries, while encouraging entrepreneurship and economic empowerment.

The Ministry has also introduced BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) to expand market access for products made by the target groups through various digital platforms in India and abroad. Under this initiative, products are branded as BHARAT TULIP to enhance their visibility and facilitate online sales. The programme aims to strengthen artisans' livelihoods while preserving traditional art forms and promoting India's rich craftsmanship to a wider audience.

The Official said the Ministry facilitates the participation of artisans by providing free stalls and support covering travel expenses, daily allowance, transportation of goods, and meals, including lunch and dinner. This assistance helps artisans participate in the mela and showcase their products without bearing stall rental costs and specified participation-related expenses.

Union Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale during his visit to Shilp Samagam Mela highlighted the Central Government’s commitment to the economic and social empowerment of socially vulnerable sections.

The Minister inspected stalls with a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed items, leather goods, wooden toys, bags, purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. He also visited the Food stalls serving traditional delicacies adding to the visitor experience.

Union Secretary of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant also visited the Mela.  

During his visit to Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds, the Secretary inspected stalls and interacted with the Stall Managers and visitors.

The Union Secretary was on a two days official visit to Mysuru to take comprehensive review of the Ministry’s Schemes, Programmes and Initiatives under implementation, with the State Social Welfare Department.

Shri Pant said through such initiatives, the Ministry continues to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and advance the economic empowerment of disadvantaged communities.

The Shilp Samagam Mela offered visitors an opportunity to explore India’s traditional crafts and handloom products while supporting the livelihoods of artisans.

It is pertinent to mention that during the Financial Year 2026–27, the Ministry is organizing additional SHILP SAMAGAM FAIRS At Guwahati, Dilli Haat in New Delhi, Jodhpur And Lucknow.

The Ministry and its three National Corporations will also participate in major exhibitions, including the India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 14 to 27, 2026, and the Surajkund Mela in Faridabad in February 2027.

Through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela and BHARAT TULIP, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote market access, entrepreneurship and livelihood opportunities for artisans from the target groups, while supporting the preservation and wider recognition of India's traditional arts and crafts.

2325436.title: India’s Nuclear Programme Dedicated to Peaceful Purposes, Says Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh; Nuclear Energy to Power AI-Driven Future
2325436.body_html:
Department of Atomic Energy
India’s Nuclear Programme Dedicated to Peaceful Purposes, Says Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh; Nuclear Energy to Power AI-Driven Future
Dr. Homi Bhabha’s vision continues to guide India’s peaceful nuclear journey as the country advances towards energy security and clean power: Dr. Jitendra Singh
“One has to be intelligent enough to use Artificial Intelligence”, Dr. Jitendra Singh stresses responsible, human-led use of AI across sectors
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has opened critical and sensitive sectors to non-government players, creating wider opportunities for private sector participation
India targets 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047 and Net Zero emissions by 2070, with nuclear energy set to meet growing demand for reliable, clean electricity: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh has said that India’s nuclear programme is dedicated to peaceful purposes and not warfare, reaffirming the vision that has guided the country’s nuclear journey since its inception.

In an exclusive conversation on the sidelines of ‘Bloomberg Economy Forum 2026’, the Minister said nuclear energy would play an increasingly important role in meeting India’s future energy requirements, including the growing demand for reliable electricity to support Artificial Intelligence (AI) and data centres.

Recalling the vision of Dr. Homi Bhabha, the architect of India’s nuclear programme, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India had consistently pursued nuclear energy for peaceful applications and national development. The commitment to the peaceful use of nuclear technology, he said, remains central to the country’s approach as it expands its capabilities to meet emerging developmental and technological needs.

The Minister said India’s nuclear energy ambitions must be viewed in the context of its long-term development goals and clean energy commitments. With the country targeting 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047 and Net Zero emissions by 2070, nuclear energy is expected to complement other sources of power by providing a continuous and reliable supply of clean electricity.

Linking nuclear energy with the next phase of technological growth, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the expansion of Artificial Intelligence and data centres would require dependable sources of electricity capable of meeting their substantial and continuous energy needs. Nuclear energy, he said, would supplement India’s other energy programmes and contribute to meeting the power requirements of an increasingly technology-driven economy.

On the expanding role of Artificial Intelligence, the Minister said AI should be viewed as a tool applicable across sectors rather than as a domain in itself. From Space and life sciences to other areas of scientific and technological development, AI is set to become an increasingly necessary instrument. Emphasising the importance of human judgement in its application, he said, “One has to be intelligent enough to use Artificial Intelligence.”

Dr. Jitendra Singh said AI offers significant advantages across domains, but ensuring its optimal use without allowing it to be misused by individuals or other actors remains a key challenge. While regulations are in place, he said integrity at both the individual and national level is fundamental to ensuring that the technology is used responsibly. India, he added, has made appreciable efforts in this direction under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The Minister also referred to the wider opening of critical and sensitive sectors to non-government players under the Modi Government. He said the approach has expanded the scope for private sector participation in areas that were traditionally more restricted, creating opportunities for industry to contribute to technological advancement, innovation and national development.

Dr. Jitendra Singh’s remarks bring together two important dimensions of India’s development trajectory: strengthening nuclear energy as a dependable source of clean power and harnessing emerging technologies such as AI through responsible, human-led application. As India advances towards its 2047 development goals and its 2070 Net Zero commitment, reliable energy infrastructure and wider participation in strategic sectors will remain important to sustaining the country’s technological and economic ambitions.

2325428.title: 25th SCO Council of Heads of Government Meeting: Raksha Mantri calls for unified action to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism
2325428.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
25th SCO Council of Heads of Government Meeting: Raksha Mantri calls for unified action to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism
“There can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, no place for its supporters”
Connectivity must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty & territorial integrity of all countries: Shri Rajnath Singh
“SCO’s success lies in creating opportunities for youth, entrepreneurs, farmers & small businesses”
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 1:16PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Member States to make concerted efforts to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism, describing the menace as one of the gravest threats to peace and development. He was addressing the 25th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (CHG) of SCO in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 20, 2026.

“Terrorism results in the loss of innocent lives and disrupts investment & commerce. It radicalises societies and deprives youth of the opportunities they rightfully deserve. There can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, and no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to terrorists,” said Raksha Mantri.

Shri Rajnath Singh recalled the deliberations at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in August-September 2026, when Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi underlined the need for concrete steps by the Organisation on issues related to security, connectivity, and opportunity. Raksha Mantri underscored India’s belief that economic engagement should be inclusive and mutually beneficial for all Member States. “India believes that the SCO must remain efficient and steadfast in its adherence to the principles of sovereign equality, consensus, and mutual respect. A greater number of institutions does not necessarily translate into greater achievements. New mechanisms should focus on clearly identified needs, avoid duplication, and prioritise delivering practical value to Member States,” he said.

Raksha Mantri emphasised the need for the SCO to build consensus and translate it into concrete action to address the uncertain global economic environment marked by geopolitical tensions, disruptions to trade and supply chains, concerns over energy and food security, and emerging technological divides. There is a need to strengthen resilient supply chains, facilitate trade and investment, and leverage technology to drive development, he said. Stressing that the benefits of economic cooperation must reach all sections of society, he reaffirmed India’s support for the adoption of an Action Plan for the Multilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation Programme for the period 2026-2030.

Shri Rajnath Singh welcomed the decisions taken at the SCO Summit in Bishkek to establish the Universal Centre in Tashkent and the Anti-Drug Centre in Dushanbe as permanent bodies of the Organisation. Their effectiveness, he said, would depend on efficient coordination and timely execution of tasks.

Underlining the importance of connectivity for shared prosperity, Raksha Mantri stated that India supports initiatives that link markets, facilitate trade and create new avenues for development. He said that initiatives such as the International North-South Transport Corridor and the Chabahar Port can contribute significantly to connecting Central Asia with broader markets.

Shri Rajnath Singh stressed that connectivity must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries, adding that projects not founded on these principles will not be sustainable. He emphasised the need to move beyond physical connectivity by simplifying customs procedures, promoting digital documentation, improving logistics and adopting interoperable digital solutions to reduce the cost of doing business across the region.

Raksha Mantri highlighted the symposium on financing infrastructure projects in Central Asia, held in Mumbai earlier this month, and expressed gratitude to Central Asian countries and SCO partners for their active participation. He also acknowledged the organisation of the first-ever SCO Asian Economic Dialogue.

“Our success should be measured by the opportunities we create for youth, new markets we open for our entrepreneurs, technologies we make available to our farmers and small-scale business owners, and the connections we foster among societies,” said Shri Rajnath Singh.

Raksha Mantri asserted that India’s own development experience demonstrates the transformative potential of technology and innovation that drive growth and deliver solutions. He highlighted the country’s Digital Public Infrastructure, which has transformed public service delivery and enhanced financial inclusion. He added that India has built one of the world’s largest start-up ecosystems, and the nation’s emphasis on women-led development is rooted in the belief that women play a defining role in shaping the path of development.

Shri Rajnath Singh underlined that India’s global initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure contribute to affordable clean energy & climate-resilient development. He added that Mission LiFE promotes sustainable lifestyles and responsible consumption, while the Global Biofuel Alliance fosters cleaner and more sustainable energy solutions.

Raksha Mantri urged the SCO to build on the strong foundation established over the past 25 years and chart a forward-looking roadmap focused on consensus-driven cooperation and tangible outcomes. He reaffirmed India’s commitment to working closely with all Member States towards achieving these objectives. He invited Member States to participate in the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum being hosted by India later this year.

The meeting reviewed progress in multilateral economic and trade cooperation among SCO Member States and discussed measures to further strengthen cooperation in areas such as transport, finance, digital economy and social development.

The Heads of Delegation adopted the Joint Communiqué of the 25th Meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government, including the SCO budget for 2027, relevant financial and administrative decisions, and the PMTEC Action Plan for 2026-2030.

The SCO CHG is an important mechanism of the Organisation responsible for promoting economic and other areas of practical cooperation among Member States. India has been a full member of the SCO since 2017 and continues to participate actively in its various mechanisms.

May this spirit keep strengthening national development in the times to come.

2325381.title: WWF-India EIACP launches nationwide Green Diwali Campaign from 20th October to 8th November 2026; Urges Citizens to celebrate a Cracker-free Diwali
2325381.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2325381.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
WWF-India EIACP launches nationwide Green Diwali Campaign from 20th October to 8th November 2026; Urges Citizens to celebrate a Cracker-free Diwali
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 10:48AM by PIB Delhi

WWF-India’s Programme Centre – Resource Partner (PC-RP),  supported by Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, has launched a nationwide Green Diwali Campaign from 20.10.2026 to 08.11.2026, urging citizens to avoid firecrackers and celebrate a clean and green Diwali in line with Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment). The campaign will reach schools, colleges, educational institutions, resident welfare associations and local communities, with a special focus on the 130 cities covered under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP).

As part of the campaign, citizens are encouraged to take the Green Diwali Pledge to avoid firecrackers, encourage family and neighbours to do the same, use diyas and energy-efficient lights, avoid single-use plastic, segregate waste and choose local products. Educational institutions and community groups are encouraged to organise pledge drives during assemblies, classes, rallies and community meetings.

Citizens are also encouraged to take WWF-India’s Carbon Footprint Survey to understand how their daily activities and consumption contribute to their environmental footprint and identify more sustainable habits. The survey is available at: https://wwfindiawebgis.in/Carbon_Footprint/Carbon_Footprint.html. Schools, colleges, EIACP centres, community groups and individuals participating in the campaign are requested to share details of their activities through the online form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/15hDbjbqZzeo68kNjAxeHQA_SMIQ7lUlPdvCIi-gvwdY/viewform.

Submissions should include the institution or organisation’s name and location, activity details and date, the number of participants who took the pledge, geo-tagged photographs and a brief report. Selected entries may be featured on EIACP websites and social media platforms.

Prime Minister congratulates Ravi K. Budigina on winning Silver in Men’s 100m Freestyle S13 at Asian Para Games 2026
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 10:11PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, congratulated Ravi K. Budigina on winning the Silver Medal in the Men’s 100m Freestyle S13 event at the Asian Para Games 2026.

Shri Modi lauded his determination, hard work and sporting spirit, describing the achievement as a proud moment for the nation. He wished Ravi K. Budigina continued success in the times ahead.
